Such a component could respond to moral content, to the judgment of conduct by any norm, or to the word "morally" in the prompt. We built 227 minimal pairs of short phrases, validated by five annotators, whose two versions differ in a moral standard, in another kind of norm (prudence, etiquette, aesthetics or evidence) or in a descriptive quality, and showed them to 14 open-weight models (Llama, Gemma and Qwen, 1B to 14B, base and instruction-tuned), with and without the word "morally". In every model, the heads that change the moral answer belong to an evaluation circuit the models use for every kind of normative judgment we tested: these heads carry the same share of the effect for moral as for other normative pairs (pooled ratio 1.00, 97.5% confidence interval [0.92, 1.07], with the word; 0.90, [0.84, 0.96], without it), and the models need them as much for both. The models need these heads also when nothing in the prompt asks for a judgment, and on 400 scenarios of the ETHICS benchmark, where removing them takes away 37 to 39% of the difference between acceptable and unacceptable scenarios, against 1 to 3% for ten random heads. The SAE features we located respond mostly to the word "morally" rather than to what the phrase is about. The models represent the category of a pair (the standard the annotators assigned to it): it can be read from their hidden states, and, in the eight models we tested, removing the direction that carries it weakens the moral verdict by a few percent, and more than the other verdicts in seven of them. We release the pairs, the ratings, the code, the trained SAE dictionaries and the result files.

papers.title: Sharp modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality for matrix-valued functions on spheres
papers.abstract: We prove that for every smooth positive definite matrix-valued function $g$ on the unit sphere $S^d$, \[ \int_{S^d}\tr(g(\log g-\log\E g))\dd \le\dfrac1{2d}\int_{S^d}\tr((\Delta g)\log g)\dd. \] Here $\mu$ is normalized area measure, $\E g$ is the spherical mean, and $\Delta$ is the positive spherical Laplacian. This complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality extends Beckner's sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequality, in its modified form, to matrix-valued functions independent of the matrix size. We show that both entropy and Fisher information decay exponentially under the heat flow with optimal exponent $2d$, whose proof combines the Bochner identity with a $4$th-tensor estimate in the matrix-valued setting.

papers.title: Remarks on Fourier--Mukai invariances
papers.abstract: This note proves that smoothness and Gorensteinness are Fourier--Mukai invariants for proper flat families of Noetherian algebraic spaces. Moreover, a kernel realizing such a partnership is perfect if, and only if, the families are smooth.

papers.title: Watermark Evidence under Open-Weight LLM Modification: Exact Bounds for Low-Rank Output Watermarks
papers.abstract: Open-weight language models can continue generating after their released weights are modified, while a watermark verifier still scores outputs against the original base and marked models. We study how such modifications change the evidence available to an OpenStamp-style verifier. At each shared prefix, we represent the modification as a residual in the next-token logits. We derive an exact finite-vocabulary lower bound on the expected log-likelihood-ratio evidence under a residual-span constraint, along with a sharp span-only deviation bound. We also characterize the first-order evidence shift through a covariance term with an explicit second-order remainder, and determine the residual span needed to reach a target evidence level. For sequence-level detection, we derive an exact conditional exponential-moment bound and combine it with a supermartingale argument and a distribution-free order-statistic tolerance bound. This yields a high-confidence upper bound on miss probability after attack selection on calibration data and evaluation on independent certification continuations. In experiments with OpenStamp on Llama-2-7B and Mistral-7B-v0.3, INT8 quantization and 30% pruning retain test true-positive rates of 85.6-94.8%, while 500-step LoRA fine-tuning lowers them to 28.8% and 11.6%. The covariance prediction tracks the measured mean LoRA evidence drift on both models, with no remainder-bound violations across 160,000 test prefixes. Additionally, we observe zero false positives among 500 base-model continuations per model. Through these theoretical and empirical results, the current research provides a better understanding of watermark robustness to model-editing/tuning attacks.

papers.title: Hybrid Quantum Selection of Learning Rates in Language-Model Training: Termination Criteria and an Interaction-Guided Schedule Oracle
papers.abstract: Learning-rate choices strongly affect language-model fine-tuning, but the best joint profile across layer groups is generally unknown. This paper studies quantum minimum finding for layer-group learning-rate selection within a hybrid classical-quantum training framework. It combines Durr-Hoyer minimum finding with BBHT search and compares fixed-budget and confidence-based stopping policies using a lookup oracle built from measured profile scores at fixed training checkpoints. The paper then introduces an Interaction-Guided Schedule Oracle that scores and marks joint schedules in superposition without a precomputed score table. Classical one-step loss measurements supply the main, pairwise and three-way interaction effects between layer groups. The circuit adds the effects for each schedule, compares the resulting score with the current baseline score, and marks improving schedules for amplitude amplification. Measured candidates are checked classically before acceptance. Uniform-rate training supplies the initial baseline; using schedules from classical adaptive methods as baselines for joint refinement is left for future work. In closed-loop fine-tuning of a 1.5-billion-parameter language model, each selected schedule drives the next 200 classical training steps. Benchmark accuracies lie within the range observed across five uniform-rate seeds. The results give a working example of how quantum superposition can support adaptive learning-rate selection during training; the remaining quantum limitations are discussed in the paper.

papers.title: Reflection Character Varieties in $\mathrm{SL}_{\pm}(n,\mathbb{R})$ for $2$-Perfect Labeled Truncation Polytopes
papers.abstract: A truncation polytope is a combinatorial polytope represented by a convex polytope obtained from a simplex by a finite sequence of vertex truncations. Marquis studied the deformation spaces of labeled truncation $3$-polytopes, and Choi-Lee-Marquis studied the $2$-perfect case in higher dimensions. In this paper, we consider Coxeter groups associated with non-simplex $2$-perfect labeled truncation $d$-polytopes with connected Coxeter diagrams, where $d\ge3$. For $n\ge d+1$, we study their reflection-generated representations in $\mathrm{SL}_{\pm}(n,\mathbb{R})$ satisfying Vinberg's conditions. Their images in the real GIT quotients of the full representation spaces under conjugation define the reflection character varieties. These varieties and their subspaces of strict characters are semialgebraic, and we determine their common dimension whenever strict characters exist. We also decompose these subspaces by Cartan matrix rank, show that the nonempty pieces are smooth manifolds, and compute their dimensions explicitly.

papers.title: The system of length sets of transfer Krull monoids over $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with class group $G$ and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. There are precisely nine groups (up to isomorphism) for which the set of distances of $H$ is contained in $\{1, 2\}$. For all these groups, except for $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$, the system of length sets has been written down explicitly. In this paper we close this gap and determine the system of length sets when the class group is isomorphic to $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$.

papers.title: FACE: Flow-Guided Angular Channel Estimation Framework for mmWave MIMO Systems
papers.abstract: Acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI) is essential for millimeter-wave (mmWave) multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems. However, it remains challenging due to high-dimensional channels, limited pilot observations, and measurement noise. To address these challenges, we propose flow-guided angular channel estimation (FACE), a novel channel estimation framework based on flow matching, an emerging generative modeling paradigm that learns continuous transport dynamics between probability distributions. FACE exploits the inherent angular-domain sparsity of mmWave channels and incorporates the learned flow matching model as a generative channel prior. Numerical results show that FACE consistently achieves higher channel estimation accuracy than both conventional estimators and diffusion-based generative estimator across diverse channel and system configurations. Moreover, FACE maintains high estimation accuracy with fewer pilot observations and achieves an average achievable rate close to the perfect-CSI benchmark. Compared with diffusion-based estimation, FACE requires substantially fewer sampling steps while achieving superior or comparable estimation accuracy, reducing inference time and computational cost. Overall, the proposed framework demonstrates the potential of flow matching for accurate, pilot-efficient, and computationally efficient mmWave MIMO channel estimation.

papers.title: The Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic PBC clusters
papers.abstract: We construct and solve the three-colored Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic lattices with periodic boundary conditions. We describe a self-contained procedure which uses finite quotients of orientation- preserving triangle groups to generate regular maps on compact genus-g surfaces. From these, one can extract their lattice connectivity, plaquette structure, homology cycles and Wilson sectors while implementing consistent boundary conditions. On the example of {8, 3} and {12, 3} lattices, we enumerate a selection of quotients with up to 72 vertices, which constitute the discrete steps in a finite-size scaling analysis. For the isotropic point, corresponding to the spin-liquid phase in the thermodynamic limit, we identify the ground state superselection sectors, quantify their deviation from the homogeneous {\pi} flux sector and show how the selected flux background depends on the quotient geometry. We then discuss how the resulting ground state sector degeneracies are entirely generated by physical lattice symmetries acting on both the plaquette fluxes and non-contractible Wilson loops. Finally, we study the behaviour of the finite-size two-vison gap and matter fermion correlations. We find that the gap does not decrease monotonically with increasing system size, while one still recovers the expected algebraic decay of the correlations at the isotropic point, even for the considered modest system sizes.

papers.title: Layerwise Learning-Rate Scaling in Vision Networks: Effective-Rate Identification, Power-Mean Aggregation, and Budget Dependence
papers.abstract: Layerwise learning-rate scaling assigns different learning rates to different parts of a network. Although established in fine-tuning pretrained models, its effects in vision networks trained from scratch are commonly assessed by training each candidate recipe. We show that, in this setting, the rate-related component of a layerwise strategy is well summarized by an effective learning rate computable directly from its multiplier profile. Across matched-control comparisons, changes in test accuracy closely track changes in training loss (r = -0.996), which supports an optimization-progress explanation of the short-budget rate effect. Increasing the untuned base learning rate tenfold shifts the rate-matched contrast upward in all six tested architectures (p = 0.016) and increases the number of architectures in which a published discriminative schedule, excluded from model fitting, outperforms the uniform control from two to five of six (p = 0.031). Within the evaluated strategy space, a parameter-weighted power mean with exponent 0.35 (95% confidence interval [0.20, 0.50]) accounts for 42.6% of within-architecture variance, compared with 36.4% for the arithmetic mean. Ranking candidates by this scalar without training improves the selected candidate's mean percentile rank from the 26th to the 10th and reduces its mean accuracy shortfall relative to the best candidate from 3.70 to 1.12 points. The rate-related effect decays as the training budget increases; relative to tuned baselines, the overall strategy effect falls within the prespecified practical-equivalence margin in two of three architectures. A separate grouping-related contrast can persist at long budgets, although its direction and magnitude depend on the architecture.

papers.title: Stop Early, Stay Simple: Evidence Acquisition for Power System Fault and Attack Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Diagnostic models for cyber-physical power systems usually inspect every telemetry source for every event, although some events are clear from one source and others need several. We ask when a learned policy for choosing that evidence is worth its added complexity. To answer this, we present ActiGrid, a benchmark framework for active evidence acquisition that pairs a classifier trained to tolerate missing modalities with a Double Deep Q-Network (DQN), which either requests another source or stops and diagnoses but never operates grid actuators. On the public TU Delft digital substation and MSU/ORNL power system attack benchmarks, we compare the DQN with fixed subsets and orders, calibrated entropy stopping, a greedy value of information rule, and tree ensembles trained per subset. The learned policy does adapt to what it observes, yet it is statistically indistinguishable from entropy stopping on TU Delft and Pareto dominated by simple controls on MSU/ORNL, while compact subset classifiers outperform it while reading fewer sources on both benchmarks. Entropy stopping run over those subset classifiers reaches the highest mean Macro-F1 on TU Delft (0.928 while reading 57% of the sources) but brings no saving over a static three source subset on MSU/ORNL, where no method exceeds 0.45 Macro-F1. Selective acquisition can pay off, but on these benchmarks it does not need a learned policy.

papers.title: TIBECG: Temporal Information Bottleneck for Lead-Specific Demographic Privacy in ECG Waveform Release
papers.abstract: Transmitting an electrocardiogram (ECG) waveform can expose demographic information beyond an intended diagnostic task. We evaluate TIBECG, an architectural temporal information bottleneck, on individual leads extracted from hospital twelve-lead recordings. A 2,302,337-parameter processor varies its latent length while retaining the same nine-score consistency objective, without age or sex labels in protector fitting. Across 6,386 recordings, ten folds, 12 leads and 21 lengths, retrospective selections retained at least 95% of each lead's clean macro-F1. Their weaker age/sex interval gain exceeded the best eligible conventional transformation on all leads, by a median 22.08 percentage points. The implemented sampling-rate comparison shows that direct downsampling usually suppresses demographic inference more strongly but at a larger loss of diagnostic utility, whereas TIBECG favors utility preservation. Selection stability also varies by lead. Lower latent Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence does not reliably rank residual sex leakage at a fixed length. These findings support lead-specific evaluation of waveform processing, not validated consumer deployment or expert-readable reconstruction. When the waveform-input diagnostic classifier is hosted as part of a proprietary cloud service rather than deployed on the device, waveform transmission is required to obtain its scores.
authors: Tsai-Min Chen (Research Center for Information Technology Innovation
RIKEN Center for Interdisciplinary Theoretical and Mathematical Sciences)
Jun Seita (RIKEN Center for Interdisciplinary Theoretical and Mathematical Sciences)

papers.title: Solution Spaces of the Minimal Surface and Monge-Amp\`{e}re Equations near Infinity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the constructions of all solutions to the minimal surface equation and the Monge-Amp\`{e}re equation near infinity and the parametrization of these solutions by harmonic functions. It is well-known that Dirichlet boundary value problems in exterior domains do not always admit solutions. We demonstrate that prescribing asymptotic behaviors forms a new type of problem leading to all solutions near infinity. The harmonic functions determining the asymptotic behaviors play the role of ``free data" as the boundary values in the boundary value problems.

papers.title: The injectivity of the Kudla--Millson lift on unitary Shimura varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the injectivity of the Kudla--Millson lift on unitary Shimura varieties over imaginary quadratic fields under some lattice hypotheses. We express integrals of the lift over special cycles as special values of Dirichlet series and deduce injectivity by separating the Fourier coefficients of the cusp forms. We also establish a converse theorem for Borcherds products on $\mathrm{U}(n,1)$.

papers.title: AdaFlowLite: Scalable and Non-blocking Inference on Asynchronous Mobile Data
papers.abstract: The rise of mobile devices equipped with numerous sensors, such as LiDAR and cameras, has driven the adoption of multi-modal deep intelligence for distributed sensing tasks, such as smart cabins and driving assistance. However, the arrival time of mobile sensory data vary due to modality size and network dynamics, which can lead to delays (if waiting for slow data) or accuracy decline (if inference proceeds without waiting). Moreover, the diversity and dynamic nature of mobile systems exacerbate this challenge. In response, we present a shift to \textit{opportunistic} inference for asynchronous distributed multi-modal data, enabling inference as soon as partial data arrives. While existing methods focus on optimizing modality consistency and complementarity, known as modal affinity, they lack a \textit{computational} approach to control this affinity in open-world mobile environments. % \sysname pioneers the formulation of structured cross-modality affinity in mobile contexts using a hierarchical analysis-based normalized matrix. This approach accommodates the diversity and dynamics of modalities, generalizing across different types and numbers of inputs. Employing an multi-modal lightweight Swin Transformer (MMLST), \sysname facilitates real-time and flexible data imputation, adapting to various modalities and downstream tasks without retraining. Experiments show that \sysname significantly reduces inference latency by up to 80.4\% and enhances accuracy by up to 62.1\%, while achieving nearly a 50\% reduction in energy consumption, outperforming status quo approaches. Also, this method can enhance LLM performance to preprocess asynchronous data.

papers.title: EgoLink: Egocentric Language-Vision Interactive Network Knowledge Challenge Summary
papers.abstract: The EgoLink Challenge at ACM Multimedia 2026 benchmarks egocentric multimodal intelligence linking first-person perception, social reasoning, and interactive action. Unlike benchmarks centered on visible objects and activities, EgoLink evaluates whether models can interpret emotional and social cues, resolve visually grounded references, and convert user requests into verified tool-mediated actions. Its two tracks cover social reasoning in egocentric video and interactive agents that complete service tasks through dialogue, tool use, and closed-loop execution. Together, they test whether perception, reasoning, and decision-making remain coupled under both offline question answering and state-changing interaction. We highlight a multi-stage Track 1 data pipeline for multiple-choice question (MCQ) generation, chain-of-thought generation, automatic quality grading, and video-contribution filtering. We summarize the task design, evaluation metrics, rules, leaderboards, and representative solutions. The benchmark combines objective answer scoring with process- and result-based evaluation, enabling analysis of both final correctness and execution quality. The best Track 1 system achieved 0.9263 accuracy, while the best Track 2 system achieved 0.844 joint success and 0.916 micro accuracy. Participant reports reveal a shared principle: strong systems make intermediate evidence explicit through candidate verification, option-robust reasoning, scenario-aware planning, tool canonicalization, and state-aware correction before answering or acting. These findings highlight the importance of process verification and evidence-grounded reasoning for reliable egocentric multimodal intelligence.

papers.title: A Critical Appraisal and Motivated Intruder Test of A Search Dataset Anonymised for the Purposes of the EU Digital Markets Act
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the European Commission's anonymisation measures for Alphabet's search-data sharing under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act against European Data Protection Board guidance and contemporary practice, and assessed re-identification through motivated intruder testing. The measures focus on search end-users, leaving other individuals mentioned in queries insufficiently protected, and do not explicitly address inference. The accompanying controls and safeguards reflect good practice for managing residual risk. Motivated intruder testing targeted 98,501 individuals across six countries using publicly available profiles. Google-verified matches yielded a re-identification rate of 0.094%, below the study's 0.47% per-team threshold. Each verified match required about three hours (Euro 105), excluding Google verification and Gemini costs, suggesting limited cost deterrence. All country-level rates were below the threshold, but one region exceeded it. The threshold drew on conservative precedents, adjusted for data quality, verification, controls and safeguards, assuming five independent attack teams. Some sensitivity scenarios exceeded the threshold, but relied on strong assumptions, such as treating all uncertain matches as correct. Results may not generalise beyond the targeted population, and ethics requirements constrained the attacks. Personal data detection recall was assumed rather than tested: the minimum defensible recall was 0.88, with 0.976 recommended. However, missed identifiers outside the allow-list would remain in the dataset. Under the study's contextual framework, assumptions and testing limitations, identity-disclosure risk was considered insignificant. This finding does not resolve the gaps concerning inference and other individuals' information; safeguards remain necessary.

papers.title: DeltaHarness: Self-Evolving Harnesses for Resource-Adaptive Tool Execution
papers.abstract: Tool-using agents rely on execution harnesses to organize and schedule tool operations. The same task and resource description can conceal runtime conditions that reverse the latency ordering of valid execution plans. Resolving this uncertainty requires firsthand execution in the target setting. We introduce DeltaHarness, an execution-guided policy-search method that adapts agent harnesses from cold-start measurements. Its QHI loop uses the observed response to update runtime dispatch, revise physical plans, and select experiments for later proposals. An independent confirmation panel controls policy replacement. With fixed dispatch, a revised materialization policy reduces complete-delivery latency by 30.0% on one video-editing task across three fresh pairs. On held-out tasks, the evolved policies reduce latency by 8.2% relative to the best fixed plan in one seed and by 4.6% relative to the initial proposal in another.

papers.title: Different Stories: European Astronomy as a Tool of Colonization in the Americas and Hawai'i
papers.abstract: The history of Western astronomy is frequently told as a story of discovery, technological innovation, and human progress. Yet the astronomical knowledge, instruments, and techniques associated with these achievements also contributed to European colonial expansion. Through four material and visual examples - a marine chronometer, an astronomical surveying quadrant, the Nautical Almanac, and contemporary observatories on Maunakea - we invite reconsideration of astronomy's relationships with navigation, territorial mapping, colonial authority, and Indigenous lands. How might these histories be told differently when considered through Indigenous Knowledges and Perspectives? What might such reconsideration reveal about the continuing relationships between astronomy, colonialism, and place?

papers.title: Mass-conservative voxelisation of smoothed particles using cumulative kernels
papers.abstract: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations are frequently post-processed on Cartesian grids for applications such as radiative transfer calculations, visualisation, and data analysis. While numerous voxelisation algorithms have been proposed, relatively little attention has been paid to the fundamental properties that such algorithms should satisfy. We argue that SPH voxelisation algorithms should accurately reproduce the underlying density field, conserve mass globally, remain consistent under grid refinement, and be computationally efficient. We present a new finite-volume algorithm designed to satisfy these requirements simultaneously. Starting from a finite-volume formulation of the SPH density field, we derive a simple expression for the mass contained in a Cartesian voxel in terms of a cumulative kernel function. The cumulative kernel is tabulated numerically once for any compact-support smoothing kernel, independently of its analytical form, so that the same tabulation and voxelisation machinery applies unchanged to any such kernel. During voxelisation, the mass contributions are obtained from interpolated evaluations of this precomputed function at voxel corners, with values at corners shared by neighbouring voxels evaluated only once and reused. We compare the new cumulative-kernel algorithm to nearest-grid-point assignment, centre sampling, regular subsampling, and Monte Carlo integration, using direct high-order numerical integration as a reference for the voxel densities, and implement it in the 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer code SKIRT. The cumulative-kernel algorithm reproduces the reference voxel densities substantially more accurately than the sampling-based methods considered. For the adopted $129^3$ cumulative-kernel lookup table (abridged).

papers.title: CSS circuits are ICM circuits without magic states
papers.abstract: Gidney and Jones recently introduced ``CSS circuits'', generated by $X$, $Z$, $\MX$, $\MZ$ and CNOT, and showed that they can be sampled with $O(1)$ work per gate. They suspected that the class had been seen before. We point out that it is, up to a normal form, the initialisation--CNOT--measurement (ICM) form introduced in 2015 for compiling fault-tolerant circuits, restricted to $\ket{0}$ and $\ket{+}$ initialisations. The ICM construction answers constructively their question about ``non-CSS-ness as a resource'': every Clifford$+T$ circuit compiles to a CSS circuit acting on $\ket{Y}$ and $\ket{A}$ input states.

papers.title: Covariance Cells And Star Products
papers.abstract: In classical statistics, a localized preparation is described not only by a point in phase space but also by a covariance cell specifying its finite resolution. We study balanced Gaussian cells on a linear symplectic space and show that they are equivalent to compatible complex structures and positive Lagrangian polarizations. Their parameter space is the Siegel symmetric space. Using the Koopman-von Neumann representation of classical mechanics, we describe the linearized transport of Gaussian amplitudes along a reference motion. Each covariance cell determines a separated star product whose antisymmetric part is fixed by the symplectic form and whose symmetric part is fixed by the covariance. This product is related to the Moyal product by Gaussian smoothing. Quadratic Hamiltonians act through their classical Poisson derivations within a fixed cell algebra exactly when they preserve the cell; squeezing transformations instead relate the algebras associated with different cells. Fronsdal's star-polarization construction yields a module whose cyclic element is the Gaussian density of the cell. Its completion is the corresponding Bargmann-Fock space, naturally embedded in the space of classical Koopman amplitudes. Koopman transport carries this Fock space to that of the transported cell. No Planck constant is introduced: the deformation parameter is a classical resolution scale, and physical observables remain commuting multiplication operators.

papers.title: When Do Tensor Product Paths Matter? A Group-Theoretic Analysis of Equivariant Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Tensor-product (TP) layers in equivariant interatomic potentials encode angular interactions through symmetry-allowed paths. Yet local site symmetry can make an allowed path carry no signal after neighbor aggregation. We call this effect Aggregation Cancellation. In a scalar-input first layer, equal-species neighbors on a complete site-symmetry orbit share scalar and radial factors, reducing their angular contribution to a spherical-harmonic orbit sum. If the restricted degree-$l$ representation has no trivial component, this sum and the corresponding path vanish for any learned radial weight. For an ideal $O_h$ octahedral orbit, this removes the $l_\mathrm{edge}=1,2,3$ classes. Beyond the first layer, the factorisation no longer holds, so cancellation is no longer guaranteed; we instead ask whether affected paths remain less important on average. We test the two levels separately in NequIP: matched-radius TiO$_6$ probes examine first-layer cancellation, whereas a within-model CaTiO$_3$ comparison and six OMat24 models examine the importance bias. We then rank paths on training frames, choose the pruning fraction on validation frames, and evaluate frozen masks on held-out tests. At the highest evaluated fraction (60% of 174 paths), force mean absolute error (MAE) changes are 1.42%, 0.04%, and 1.83% for CaTiO$_3$, OMat24 $O_h$-cubic, and OMat24 low-symmetry data, respectively. The masks imply 67.12-71.94% potential TP-operation reduction and 59.77% potential edge multilayer perceptron (MLP) reduction; these are structural proxies, not measured speedups. The results connect local symmetry to path redundancy and pruning robustness in NequIP; transfer to other architectures remains open.

papers.title: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six LLMs were evaluated, with overall accuracy ranging from 34.0% to 73.9% across three distinct performance tiers. To assess reasoning quality, an LLM-based judge evaluated correctly answered responses using a multidimensional rubric. Although responses generally demonstrated strong problem comprehension, they scored lower in factual and procedural accuracy and distractor analysis, indicating that correct answers were not necessarily supported by technically sound justifications. Response clarity was also weakly indicative of technical quality. Furthermore, longer reasoning traces were associated with lower accuracy in both frontier reasoning models, suggesting that reasoning length may reflect question difficulty rather than improved problem-solving performance. Reasoning-token consumption may therefore provide an additional signal for identifying potentially unreliable responses. NEBench R1 establishes a benchmark for evaluating both answer accuracy and reasoning quality, providing a foundation for assessing the domain competence and reliability of LLMs in nuclear engineering.

papers.title: Remark on internal relaxation in large number qubit systems
papers.abstract: For a time $t_{c}$ of calculation in an $N$ qubit quantum computer that is much shorter than the intrinsic Heisenberg time $t_H$, $t_c\ll t_H$, the dynamics of the system is effectively irreversible and the couplings between the qubits give rise to a relaxation time scale $\tau_r$. If $t_H\gg t_c >\sim \tau_r$ one looses quantum coherence exponentially fast. Since $t_H$ scales exponentially with $N$ there is a threshold $N_c$ such that for $N\gg N_c$ one must be aware of possible intrinsic relaxation during calculation. As an order of magnitude estimation we find $N_c\approx \ln(\tau_r/T)$ where $T$ is a typical system specific oscillation time of a single qubit. $\tau_r$ can be estimated as the typical inverse transition rate between two parts of the system, one of which is treated as an environment of the other.

papers.title: Edge-Adaptive Hiera-Seg Model for Building-Integrated Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
papers.abstract: Building integrated photovoltaic power forecasting is challenging because facade orientation, rooftop geometry, nearby buildings, vegetation, cloud movement, module temperature, inverter status and edge device reliability jointly affect power generation. This paper proposes an edge-adaptive HieraSeg model for short term BIPV power forecasting with multi-orientation visual-irradiance fusion. RGB facade images, optional thermal cues, irradiance measurements, module temperature, facade orientation, rooftop masks, shading labels, sky condition, historical power and edge device state are aligned into synchronous forecasting windows. HieraSeg extracts hierarchical regions from facade, rooftop, sky, shadow and background images, while the edge-adaptive module changes feature weights under missing frames, latency shifts and local shading changes. The segmentation branch identifies occluded module areas and separates facade, rooftop, sky and background evidence before the forecasting head estimates future BIPV output. Experiments are designed on a simulated multibuilding BIPV dataset with unseen building and unseen orientation tests. The model reports predicted power, confidence interval, dominant evidence, occlusion contribution, orientation contribution and energy-management review priority. This output is intended to show whether the forecast is driven by irradiance change, visible shading, orientation response, stale edge information or recent power history. The framework supports local forecasting at edge controllers with limited communication delay and computing resources, linking visual occlusion, irradiance dynamics and power history to traceable forecasting results for building energy management, microgrid scheduling and BIPV operation planning.

papers.title: FCP: Formal Context Protocol for Verifying LLM-Generated Artifacts
papers.abstract: When a language model writes both an artifact and the tests meant to check it, a passing test is weak evidence: one misreading of the request yields a faulty artifact and a check that accepts it. We present the Formal Context Protocol (FCP), which checks AI-generated artifacts against the request itself. FCP separates conformance (does the artifact satisfy a formal reading of a requirement?), which model checkers and SMT solvers decide, from fidelity (does the reading mean what the prose means?), which has no decision procedure but is refutable by a concrete witness. Eight ways a proof can falsely certify a requirement each become a mechanical check that returns a witness, and what no machine can settle becomes concrete questions for the request's author. Adapters place hardware, text, agents and code on the same engines. On four hardware designs, trusting AI-written assertions certified 23% of violated requirements, and FCP certified none. On ten code tasks, code from three language models passed its own tests and violated the request every time. Trusting the tests certified all 33 violations, and FCP certified three. Agreement among models, readings or tests did not imply correctness.

papers.title: RTLReviewBench: LLM Hardware Reviewers Rarely Miss Bugs but Routinely Reject Correct RTL
papers.abstract: Hardware teams increasingly ask large language models (LLMs) to review register-transfer level (RTL) code, yet it is unclear whether a model can tell a correct module from a buggy one without simulating it. We introduce RTLReviewBench, a benchmark of 114 matched pairs of buggy and correct Verilog modules. Each pair shares one specification, most buggy modules are real failures of LLM code generators, and every label is confirmed by simulation. Evaluating 12 commercial and open-weight models, we find a consistent asymmetry: reviewers rarely accept buggy code but often reject correct code, producing more than five false rejections for every missed bug. Synthetic mutants hide part of the problem: on the same designs, models miss far fewer injected bugs than real ones. Asking a model to reason before it commits to a verdict sharply reduces false rejections for weaker reviewers, and a controlled ablation shows that where the reasoning appears in the output matters more than the instruction to reason, whereas sampling and majority voting do not help. A blinded audit further shows that some correct "buggy" verdicts rest on false technical claims. We release the benchmark, a harder split for future models, all model responses, and the evaluation code at https://github.com/yasirmahmud/RTLReviewBench

papers.title: Chimera: A Configurable LLM Decode Accelerator Architecture with Compute-Memory-Floorplan Co-Design for HBM-Equipped Multi-Die FPGAs
papers.abstract: GPUs are widely used for LLM inference, but single-request decoding is memory-bound, leaving their compute underutilized while they draw substantial power. HBM-equipped FPGAs are well suited to LLM decoding: their customizable datapaths use memory bandwidth more energy-efficiently than GPUs. However, high memory bandwidth alone does not ensure high decode performance: exploiting it requires parallel compute and memory interfaces, whose resource costs and placement on the chip can limit the throughput. We present Chimera, a configurable LLM decode accelerator architecture that co-designs compute, memory access, and floorplan. Specifically, HBM Proxy Ports extend HBM access to compute lanes on every super logic region (SLR) die, and tiered expert storage holds mixture-of-experts weights beyond the HBM capacity. In addition, a unified configuration analysis estimates per-token latency and per-SLR resource use and guides the design of each configuration within resource budgets. On an AMD Alveo U280, we build ten designs for eight dense, mixture-of-experts, hybrid linear/standard-attention, and ternary LLMs, up to an 80B-parameter mixture-of-experts LLM on four memory tiers. Chimera's designs achieve a geometric mean of 1.6$\times$ the token throughput of prior state-of-the-art FPGA implementations and 3.0$\times$ and 1.5$\times$ the energy efficiency of the RTX 3090 and A100 GPUs, setting a new benchmark for LLM decoding on HBM-equipped FPGAs.

papers.title: Renormalization-Group Foundation of Critical Modes in Correlation Matrices
papers.abstract: Based on the relevant scaling operators of renormalization-group theory, we establish a theoretical framework for constructing complete families of critical-sensitive fluctuation observables and their connected correlation matrices. The corresponding eigenstates of the correlation matrices reveal a hierarchy of multiscale critical correlation patterns and the leading normalized eigenvalues and their ratios show the finite-size scaling behavior. Applying this framework to the two-dimensional Ising model, the correlation matrices associated with both spin and energy operators are constructed. The resulting energy-sector eigenstate patterns, together with the scaling behavior of the leading eigenvalues, provide further support for the proposed framework. Finally, we discuss its potential extension to systems with unknown Hamiltonians.

papers.title: Statistical Properties of the $q$-Deformed Monolayer and Bilayer Graphene
papers.abstract: We investigate the statistical properties of the $q$-deformed Dirac oscillator for monolayer and bilayer graphene in the presence of a constant external magnetic field. Using $q$-deformed creation and annihilation operators, we obtain the corresponding energy spectra and eigenfunctions, as well as their probability current densities, recovering the conventional Landau-level structures in the undeformed limit. For bilayer graphene, the lowest Landau levels are explicitly constructed within the $q$-deformed framework. The partition functions for both systems are derived using zeta-function techniques and the Euler-Maclaurin formula, allowing us to determine their main thermodynamic quantities for small values of the deformation parameter. Our results show that the $q$-deformation modifies the energy spectra, the behavior of the probability current density components, and the thermodynamic response of the systems. A comparison between monolayer and bilayer graphene reveals distinct thermal behaviors, reflecting their different Landau-level structures and highlighting the influence of the $q$-deformation on their statistical properties.

papers.title: Improving Early Detection of Scientifically Interesting Radio Sources Using Enhanced Isolation Forest
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of radio astronomical surveys has created a major challenge in identifying scientifically interesting sources from large populations of observed objects. This study investigates whether enhanced Isolation Forest (iForest) methods can improve the early detection and ranking of scientifically interesting radio sources. Four iForest variants, Standard Enhanced, Pooled Gain, Kurtosis-based, and Hypervolume, are evaluated using 1,031 extended radio sources from the MeerKAT Galaxy Cluster Legacy Survey (MGCLS). Each source is represented by a 52-dimensional feature set derived using Bootstrap Your Own Latent (BYOL) self-supervised learning and principal component analysis (PCA), while expert scientific-interest ratings are used to define the ground-truth labels. The methods are evaluated using Average Precision (AP), receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC), Precision@10, Precision@50, and cumulative anomaly detection. Pooled Gain achieves the highest Average Precision (AP = 0.201) and the strongest early-stage ranking performance (P@10 = 0.600), identifying six expert-validated anomalies among the ten highest-ranked sources. Standard Enhanced and Kurtosis-based achieve the highest ROC AUC (0.677), while the AUC values of the four variants range from 0.653 to 0.677. These results indicate that feature-aware isolation strategies can improve the prioritization of scientifically interesting sources at the top of the ranked list, although overall discrimination remains comparable across the evaluated variants. The findings support the use of enhanced Isolation Forest methods as an initial ranking mechanism within human-in-the-loop systems for large-scale radio astronomical surveys.

papers.title: Gallai's path decomposition conjecture for $K_5$-minor-free graphs
papers.abstract: Gallai conjectured that the edges of every connected graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into at most $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. We prove that every connected $K_5$-minor-free graph other than $K_3$ and $K_5-e$ admits such a partition into at most $\floor{n/2}$ paths. The two exceptions require $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. In a smallest counterexample we find a $4$-connected planar part containing four vertices of degree five. Their neighborhoods meet the boundary in at most one vertex. This allows us to apply the planar configurations of Blanch\'e, Bonamy, and Bonichon and to realize the reduced graph as a minor of the original graph.

papers.title: Who sees the sea? Sea-view potential by fa\c{c}ade and floor from cadastral LoD1 models on the Costa del Sol
papers.abstract: Views are among the most valued and least measured attributes of a home. We present an open-data method that estimates the sea-view potential of every free fa\c{c}ade of every residential building at three floors (ground, middle and top; other floors take the nearest of them), from cadastral footprints with floor counts and a national terrain model. Run for 158,060 buildings of 21 municipalities on Spain's Costa del Sol in under an hour on two cores, it finds that 52 % of buildings see some sea from their top floor and 36 % have an open view (20{\deg} or more). Traced over a LiDAR surface in a pilot, scores agree with the model's inside cadastral footprints (96.7 % of viewpoints in the same class at 20{\deg}), but structures the cadastre does not record lower the sea seen from the top floor by 6.1--9.0{\deg} on average. Against the photographs of 93 homes for sale, labelled blind by AI models of two developers with ties decided by the author, the score has an AUC of 0.80 (95 % CI 0.70--0.89; 0.81 against the first-round labels); at 20{\deg} it is sensitive (0.90) but not specific (0.45). Dwelling figures depend on how dwellings are allocated to fa\c{c}ades and floors: 42 % of dwellings are on a floor with open-view potential under the main rule, and 12--45 % across the allocation, geometry and vegetation scenarios tested. As an application, higher-income census sections tend to have more modelled view potential within municipalities, with uncertain size and fragile inference (about two effective clusters); on terrain alone the difference largely disappears. Code and fa\c{c}ade-level data reproduce the main results.

papers.title: A Riemann-invariant contact-capturing scheme with WENO reconstruction and RH-motivated dual-speed dissipation for compressible two-phase mixture flows
papers.abstract: This work develops and benchmarks centred (Riemann-solver-free) finite-volume fluxes for a hyperbolic two-phase mixture model with velocity non-equilibrium. The baseline method combines a Riemann-invariant contact-capturing algorithm (RICCA) with dual-speed dissipation and primitive-variable WENO3/WENO5 reconstruction, avoiding full eigen-decomposition while retaining a conservative update. An RH-motivated companion flux (RICCA--RH) is introduced, in which the acoustic weight in $\alpha = |V_n| + Ba$ is controlled by a binary pressure/Rankine--Hugoniot switch. On one-dimensional gas--magma Riemann suite, RICCA--RH tracks legacy RICCA and is sharper than first-order FORCE/Lax--Friedrichs at material contacts; a linearised spectral study clarifies how its dual-speed dissipation differs from FORCE. With WENO5, RICCA, RICCA--RH and FORCE produce essentially identical smooth profiles, indicating that most differences are confined to first-order contact metrics. In two dimensions (gas--liquid benchmarks), the production flux implemented on CPU and Apple Metal reproduces expansion-tube, collision and forward-facing-step patterns and yields intermediate cut-based roughness between RICCA and FORCE. High order is obtained using an approximate face-normal acoustic characteristic reconstruction, a pragmatic multi-variable hybrid sensor, and a Zhang--Shu-style invariant-domain face limiter on $(\rho,\alpha,c)$. An under-dissipative soft-switch variant that rings severely is also documented, and a resident 2D Metal kernel on Apple Silicon is reported to deliver up to $3.9\times$ wall-clock speedup on completed CPU/Metal comparisons (peak on the $101\times101$ expansion tube).

papers.title: Resistance-regular graphs need not be regular
papers.abstract: A connected graph is resistance-regular if the sum of the effective resistances from a vertex to all other vertices does not depend on the vertex, or equivalently if the Moore-Penrose inverse of its Laplacian has constant diagonal. Walk-regular graphs have this property, and Zhou, Wang and Bu asked in 2016 whether every resistance-regular graph is regular, a question that also arises in the study of graphs with constant resistance curvature. We answer this question in the negative and examine both what resistance-regularity forces and how far from regular such graphs can be. On the spectral side, we prove that a connected graph is walk-regular if and only if the first $m-1$ powers of its Laplacian pseudoinverse have constant diagonal, where $m$ is the number of distinct nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues. Because resistance-regularity constrains only the first power, it forces regularity when $m\le2$ and allows at most two vertex degrees when $m=3$. Any non-regular resistance-regular graph has minimum degree at least $3$ and a connected complement, and an exhaustive computer search shows that it must have at least $13$ vertices. For every even $p\ge4$, we construct a resistance-regular graph on $4p$ vertices with degrees $2p-2$ and $2p-1$, obtaining closed formulas for its Laplacian spectrum and for all pairwise effective resistances. Using module blow-ups, we then construct $n$-vertex resistance-regular graphs whose two degrees differ by $(\sqrt{4n+1}-5)/4$ for infinitely many $n$, as well as examples with three and four distinct degrees, whereas the maximum and minimum degrees of any resistance-regular graph on $n$ vertices differ by less than $n/2$. We close by conjecturing that in a resistance-regular graph the sum of squared resistances at a vertex increases strictly with its degree.

papers.title: Token Commitment as a Control Surface for Steering Masked Diffusion Generation
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models repeatedly predict provisional tokens before a sampler decides which predictions become permanent. Existing inference-time steering methods primarily modify activations, logits, or denoising trajectories, while treating this commitment policy as a fixed decoding detail. We instead study token commitment as a diffusion-specific control surface and separate it into two decisions: which tokens to commit and how many tokens to commit at each step. For the first, we introduce counterfactual target-aware commitment, which ranks unresolved positions by a mixture of model confidence and leave-one-token-out target contribution. For the second, we introduce calibrated adaptive budgets driven by target progress and confidence. Across language and vision-language settings in the LLaDA family, multiple targets, two activation-steering methods, and an unsteered control, both mechanisms yield empirically monotonic target-quality trade-offs in every configuration we evaluate. Adaptive schedules also recover competitive operating points relative to scorer-free stochastic schedules matched in average denoising cost. Because both mechanisms require only a scalar score evaluated on a provisional completion, they apply unchanged when the target is an automatic proxy for task success rather than an output attribute: NLI entailment for dialogue summarization and CLIPScore for captioning, neither of which corresponds to a single reusable steering direction. We reproduce the behavior of both mechanisms on a second masked-diffusion family, Dream-7B, for one control target and one task-success target. These results characterize commitment--which provisional predictions become irreversible, and how rapidly--as an interpretable control surface for steering masked diffusion generation under the conditions we test.

papers.title: Multiobjective household energy planning using evolutionary algorithms
papers.abstract: This article presents the advances in the design and implementation of a recommendation system for planning the use of household appliances, focused on improving energy efficiency from the point of view of both energy companies and end-users. The system proposes using historical information and data from sensors to define instances of the planning problem considering user preferences, which in turn are proposed to be solved using a multiobjective evolutionary approach, in order to minimize energy consumption and maximize quality of service offered to users. Promising results are reported on realistic instances of the problem, compared with situations where no intelligent energy planning are used (i.e., Bussiness as Usual model) and also with a greedy algorithm developed in the framework of the reference project. The proposed evolutionary approach was able to improve up to 29.0% in energy utilization and up to 65.3% in user preferences over the reference methods.

papers.title: Michelson and Logarithmic Operator Contrasts Spectral Geometry, Tracial Extensions, and Random Products
papers.abstract: The Michelson contrast of a positive invertible operator is a bounded coordinate for its condition number. Its logarithmic lift, $\operatorname{OLC}(A)=\frac12\log(\|A\|\|A^{-1}\|)$, connects spectral spread with projective Thompson geometry. This preprint collects the Novikov--Nikolaeva series and the associated single-author extensions by Novikov into one treatment. We develop the equality criterion for product subadditivity, its dimension and Jordan-rank thresholds, quantum-state examples, and contrasts associated with unitarily invariant norms. The latter have a sharp additive defect, while the full Schatten family records a logarithmic spectral profile up to homometry. Tracial extensions give characterisations of traces, dimension-sensitive defects, and spectral-edge asymptotics. Unbounded operators are described through critical exponents and finite sections. Tensor, matrix and free independence lead to distinct growth laws for products. Finally, symmetric cones provide a setting for the equality criterion, Lorentz boosts, and Jordan products. Classical ingredients are distinguished from the refinements developed in the series; conjectural asymptotic statements remain explicitly labelled.

papers.title: Testyard Benchmarks: a Dynamic RISC-V-based Benchmark Framework including DfT insertion, Structural and Functional Test Flows
papers.abstract: The main challenge of modern computing manufacturing is to produce silicon products capable of operating under the worst possible conditions, both in data centers and under stringent functional safety constraints. These requirements impose exceptionally high quality standards on silicon vendors, while testing costs keep escalating as transistors continue to shrink. Evaluating new testing strategies, however, presents a dual challenge for researchers. Standard academic benchmarks, such as the ITC-99 suite, remain valuable for fast test prototyping, but they lack the structural complexity of modern VLSI devices. Assessing the true computational effort of academic methodologies on industrial scale designs is equally difficult without accessible and scalable models. A further obstacle is the absence of a unified framework able to abstract the commands imposed by each EDA tool and the configurations tied to each technology library, forcing researchers to spend time adapting and debugging fragile scripts. This work addresses both needs by proposing the Testyard framework, built on top of the Chipyard framework, to derive a set of open-source, industrial scale benchmarks. It also extends the Hammer VLSI flow abstraction framework with hardware testing capabilities. Three new functionalities are introduced into Hammer: Design-for-Testability (DfT) insertion, ATPG, and functional tests fault simulation. Each functionality is driven by high-level descriptions, while the framework translates these inputs into the commands required by each EDA tool. The extended framework is applied to 13 representative SoC configurations from the Chipyard ecosystem, reporting the first comprehensive structural and functional test results across three technology libraries and multiple fault models, including stuck-at, transition delay, and small delay faults.

papers.title: A Proof of the Achlioptas-Friedgut Convergence Conjecture
papers.abstract: For every fixed integer $q\ge3$, we show that the $q$-colourability transition in a sparse random graph takes place at a limiting edge density, thus proving the Achlioptas-Friedgut convergence conjecture. The proof adapts the argument we recently introduced to settle the satisfiability conjecture.

papers.title: Co-edge-regular graphs with two $\lambda$-values and four distinct eigenvalues
papers.abstract: A connected $k$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is co-edge-regular if any two distinct non-adjacent vertices have the same number of common neighbors. For adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$, let $\lambda(u,v)=|N(u)\cap N(v)|$. Ge and Koolen asked whether the theorem of Neumaier on strongly regular graphs with fixed smallest eigenvalue extends to co-edge-regular graphs with exactly four distinct eigenvalues in which $\lambda(u,v)$ takes exactly two values over the edges $uv$. In this paper, we answer this question. For every integer $t\ge2$ there is $n_t$ such that if $G$ is such a graph with smallest eigenvalue at least $-t$, $n\ge n_t$, and $k<n-2-(t-1)^2/4$, then either $G$ is a clique extension of a strongly regular graph, or $G$ is obtained from a strongly regular graph with a Hoffman coloring by adding all edges inside the color classes. Consequently, $G$ is a clique extension of a strongly regular graph, a $p\times q$ grid with $p\ne q$, or the block graph of a resolvable Steiner $2$-design in which every parallel class is made into a clique.

papers.title: Multicore Quantum Architecture for Scalable and Energy-Aware Green IoT Computing
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) is increasing the computational demand placed on edge and backend processing infrastructures, motivating scalable architectures that can reduce execution and communication overhead. This paper presents a communication-aware comparison of homogeneous multicore classical and quantum architectures for Green IoT using the Qcomm simulator. In addition, a mesh-based, homogeneous, quantum-classical multicore architecture is proposed to enable scalable, efficient execution of distributed quantum workloads. We evaluate a 4x4 mesh of 16 processing cores under regular, classical-bottleneck, and quantum-bottleneck conditions, and study the effects of traffic pattern and Light-to-Matter (LTM) port provisioning on performance. Results show that butterfly traffic yields the largest gains over uniform traffic in both execution time and qubit coherence, while performance benefits from additional LTM ports saturate beyond four ports. At the algorithm level, homogeneous Multi Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) achieve 10x, 9x, and 7x energy efficiency improvements in comparison to Multi-CPUs for Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and Quantum Neural Network (QNN), respectively. The paper's findings show that communication-aware multicore quantum architectures are promising for latency-sensitive IoT processing. Furthermore, the results validate the proposed architecture and provide a foundation for future scheduling and resource management techniques to improve scalability and efficiency in multi-QPU systems.

papers.title: The Mechanics of Curvature Inflation
papers.abstract: We examine slow roll directly in the Jordan-frame Hubble equation. For the quadratic Starobinsky action, this equation has an exact mechanical form. Comparing nearby solutions at the same Hubble value gives a local contraction law on the expanding branch with decreasing Hubble rate. A signed square root of the Hubble parameter also continues the vacuum background smoothly through its Hubble zeroes. For metric actions built from a smooth function of the Ricci scalar, coefficients depending only on the Hubble parameter require a derivative expansion. We derive the terms through cubic order and test both the equation residual and the error accumulated by an independently evolved approximation. A regularized inverse-logarithmic extension provides a nontrivial example. On the parameter slice studied, we prove a positive lower bound on the second curvature derivative of the action and compare separate Jordan- and Einstein-frame integrations. The third-order approximation reproduces the exact inflationary trajectory more accurately than the second-order approximation over the interval tested. We also compute the linear scalar and tensor spectra with numerical convergence checks. The benchmark gives a scalar spectral index of 0.97384 and a tensor-to-scalar ratio of 0.00527, evaluated 60 exact Einstein-frame e-folds before the first acceleration exit. These values depend on the chosen action and reference event. The mechanical form supplies approximation tests for the background; the scalaron and its perturbations follow from the original gravitational action.

papers.title: A Sharp Perimeter Inequality for Mean Distances on Convex Curves
papers.abstract: For a planar convex body $K$, let $\theta(K)$ denote the expected Euclidean distance between two independent points uniformly distributed on $\partial K$ with respect to arclength. We prove the sharp inequality $$\frac{\theta(K)}{\operatorname{per}K}>\frac{1}{6}.$$ The constant is approached by rectangles degenerating to a segment.

papers.title: New Agegraphic Dark Energy in Braneworld Cosmology: A Higher Dimensional Perspective on Dark Energy Evolution
papers.abstract: In this study, we investigate the new agegraphic dark energy model within the context of braneworld cosmology. A higher dimensional viewpoint on the evolution of dark energy is examined. A combination of cold dark matter and dark energy, is explored within the frameworks of RS-II and DGP brane as the underlying gravitational theories. Both the possibilities involving interaction and non-interaction between dark energy and cold dark matter are investigated. A range of cosmological parameters, including the equation of state parameter, deceleration parameter, and statefinder parameters, are examined. The squared velocity of sound is examined to assess the system's stability. A data analysis based on observations, utilizing contemporary cosmological data and the Markov chain Monte Carlo method, is conducted to constrain the parameter space of the model. Our research suggests that the interplay between higher-dimensional phenomena and agegraphic dark energy provides a theoretically robust and observationally consistent framework for the universe's late-time acceleration.

papers.title: Gravitational memory, spin memory and S-duality at null infinity of the heterotic string
papers.abstract: We determine the asymptotic structure at future null infinity of heterotic string theory compactified on $T^6$, in the consistent truncation to the Einstein-frame metric, the axion--dilaton $\tau=a+ie^{-2\phi}$ and the gauge fields descending from ten dimensions, through first order in $\alpha'$. Three results stand out. First, the radiative data, balance laws and memory observables organize under the S-duality group of the four-dimensional theory: the scalar flux in the Bondi mass loss is the invariant metric of $SL(2,\mathbb R)/U(1)$ evaluated on the scalar news, the gauge flux is the norm of a self-dual radiation field, and at fixed vacuum the residual duality rotation acts with charges $0$, $1$ and $2$ on gravitational, electromagnetic and dilaton--axion radiation, so that S-dual processes share their gravitational waveform and memories and differ in their scalar memory. Second, the spin memory receives a gauge-field contribution whose ordinary part is fixed by the Dirac--Schwinger--Zwanziger product of the total charge with the change of the charge aspect; it is generated by mutually nonlocal dyons, and its dipole part agrees in magnitude and sign with the angular momentum radiated by a charge scattered off a magnetic monopole. Third, within the four-derivative effective action, the Gauss--Bonnet and Pontryagin couplings fixed by the Green--Schwarz mechanism leave the mass-loss and angular-momentum balance laws unchanged at first order in $\alpha'$ and first enter the evolution of the spin-two curvature coefficient, $\partial_u\Psi_0^0\supset\tfrac{3i\alpha'}{2}\tau_1\bar\Psi_4^0$, which combines dilaton and axion into the complex scalar charge aspect and is not invariant under the residual duality rotation. For black holes with fixed physical charges $\tau_1$ is of order one, so this is a first-order effect in $\alpha'/M^2$.

papers.title: New traversable wormholes without invoking exotic matter in $f(Q)$ from the freedom of different connections
papers.abstract: Wormhole solutions in General Relativity can only exist in the presence of exotic matter that violates the null energy condition. In this paper, we investigate the possibility of constructing wormhole solutions in $f(Q)$ gravity in which the extra connection degrees of freedom contribute such that no exotic matter is needed. Considering the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole as an example, we find that the system admits two families of connections consistent with the spacetime symmetries and the requirements of symmetric teleparallel gravity. For both families, we show that constant non-metricity scalar $Q$ is not merely a simplifying assumption but arises naturally from the field equations when $f_{QQ}$ is regular, and that the resulting exact analytic solutions can satisfy the null energy condition throughout the entire spacetime. For the second family, which possesses richer connection degrees of freedom, we further demonstrate that solutions with a spatially varying $Q$ exist when $f_{QQ}$ is allowed to diverge at a finite value of $Q$, and that these too can satisfy the null energy condition everywhere. Our results show that the nontrivial connection degrees of freedom in $f(Q)$ gravity can naturally be responsible for supporting wormhole geometries, without resorting to any exotic matter.

papers.title: Counting formulas and refined generating functions for inversion-sequence Classes 152 and 207
papers.abstract: For the two Class 152 pattern sets, we prove that the common number of inversion sequences of length \(n\geq 1\) is \(a_n=1+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\binom{2j}{j}\). The Class 152 proof uses first-descent and last-zero decompositions, with weighted Dyck paths evaluating the resulting generating functions. For Class 207, we prove equality of the three total-count series and give their common generating function as an explicit Lambert-series expression after the substitution \(z=q/(1+q)^2\). Complete legal-site and catalytic recurrences lead to a Lambert series for one class and \(q\)-product orbit sums for another. A cubic limit of the balanced nonterminating \({}_3\phi_2\) \(q\)-Saalschutz summation identifies these expressions. Fixed-maximum expansions, finite verification data, refined analytic obstructions, and signed specializations are recorded in the supplementary material.

papers.title: Cycles of Arbitrary Period in Multidimensional Heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study periodic behavior in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause opinion dynamics with multidimensional opinions and norm-defined confidence neighborhoods. We prove that, for every dimension $d\ge3$, every $\ell_q$ norm with $q\in[1,\infty]\setminus\{2\}$, and every integer $m\ge2$, a system of five agents admits a periodic trajectory of minimal period $m$; moreover, different periods can coexist for fixed confidence radii. Four agents remain stationary, while the fifth moves along a line segment contained in their convex hull. The stationary agents may share a common strictly positive confidence radius, and all confidence inequalities are strict. A geometric criterion underlying the construction extends these results to further classes of norms. However, this criterion cannot be satisfied in dimensions one and two, regardless of the confidence norm. We also prove that no heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause system with less than five agents admits a nonconstant periodic trajectory, under any norm and in any dimension; every trajectory with at most three agents converges exponentially.

papers.title: Depth-Aware Activation Steering via Attention Residuals
papers.abstract: Activation steering is a simple, training-free way to modulate LLM behavior, yet existing methods typically inject vectors at a single layer and lack mechanisms for depth-aware propagation or internal verification. We combine two recent ideas - Attention Residuals (AttnRes) providing learnable cross-layer pathways, and Jacobian-lens (J-space) concept readout - into a lightweight depth-aware steering pipeline. On two small open models (Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3.5-0.8B), distributing a persona vector according to AttnRes-style depth weights yields stronger internal alignment (deeper-layer concept cosine and rank, p<0.0001) and stronger behavioral shifts than single-layer injection. The effect is sign-specific: reverse vectors invert all six metrics, random directions degrade alignment (p<0.0001), and a short LoRA fine-tune erases the imprint. Injection rewires attention strictly downstream of the injection point (upstream JS = 0.00000). Three practical findings follow. First, a layer-wise geometric decomposition of cosine readouts: at the injection layer 123% of the increase is arithmetic, while 5-11 layers downstream 100% is dynamical. Second, an intensity window: effects are monotone over 0.3-0.7, then generation collapses (617 to 306 to 25 chars). Third, metric discipline: keyword-rule metrics fail LLM-judge validation (kappa <= 0.09), and two rule-based conclusions were retracted. Training the depth weights on a steering objective (200 steps, frozen backbone) raises final alignment 10x on held-out prompts. Cross-persona vectors retain 96-99% of the effect: specificity holds against random, not semantic, directions. We contribute a practical, low-overhead depth-aware steering method with a careful evaluation protocol. Code and data are released.

papers.title: Quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for Lagrangian Grassmannian
papers.abstract: We give a quantum $K$-theoretic analogue of the Whitney relation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. As a consequence, we give a presentation of the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The strategy for obtaining such relations is to use the quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for the full-flag manifold in type $C$ established by the author and Kato's pushforward map from the quantum $K$-ring of the full-flag manifold to that of the partial flag manifold. Then the Nakayama-type argument established by Gu et al., together with the classical Whitney presentation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian, gives a proof of such a presentation.

papers.title: Evaluating Semantic Insensitivity in Financial Sentiment Analysis: Implications for Sustainable Financial Decision-Making
papers.abstract: Financial sentiment analysis is critical for automated trading, portfolio management, and risk assessment, heavily relying on models like FinBERT. Despite high benchmark accuracy, these models remain vulnerable to subtle adversarial text modifications, threatening the integrity of algorithmic decision-making. In this paper, we propose Agent-driven Semantic Inversion (ASI), a novel adversarial attack framework targeting financial sentiment models through domain-specific semantic manipulation. Utilizing an LLM-powered multi-agent pipeline, our approach identifies eligible financial news sentences and applies targeted lexical substitutions. We empirically evaluate ASI against FinBERT, one of the most widely deployed financial sentiment models. Our results reveal a striking vulnerability: the attack successfully deceived FinBERT in 90.85% of eligible cases, with the model frequently maintaining its original sentiment prediction despite the fundamental inversion of financial performance indicators. Through qualitative analysis and token-level investigation, we demonstrate that FinBERT critically over-relies on contextual keywords and syntactic patterns rather than true logical comprehension of financial semantics. Our findings highlight the urgent need for logic-aware, robust financial NLP models to ensure the reliability of automated decision-making systems.

papers.title: Exact solution of the two-dimensional one-component plasma on the truncated Beltrami pseudosphere
papers.abstract: We solve exactly the two-dimensional one-component plasma at coupling $\Gamma=2$ on the truncated Beltrami pseudosphere, a surface of constant negative curvature bounded by two parallels. A conformal map onto a flat cylinder leaves the particles interacting through the flat-cylinder potential, with the curvature entering only through the area element. The partition function becomes a product of incomplete gamma functions, the density is explicit, and all correlations are determinantal. Since the area is bounded, the large-N limit is taken at fixed shape. The free energy, obtained through the constant term with every coefficient in closed form, contains a bulk term (1/2)N ln N, a term linear in N, the flat hard-wall surface tension times the total boundary length, and a shape-dependent constant, with no ln N term. This is the conformal-anomaly prediction for Euler characteristic zero, tested here on a surface where the integrated Gaussian and boundary curvatures are separately nonzero and cancel. The expansion coincides term by term with the cylinder result of Shen and Forrester, whose universal constants are quadratures of the two boundary layers. At both walls the density tends to the flat contact value $n_b$ ln 2, from opposite sides, although the circumferences differ by a factor cosh u_max. We compare the asymptotics with the exact solution up to N=4096, and Monte Carlo simulations at $\Gamma= $1, 4 and 6, validated against the exact $\Gamma= $ 2 density, show how the boundary layers evolve with coupling.

papers.title: Consistency Is Not Correction: Separating Confidence, Abstention, and Recovery in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: A controller that resamples an answer, escalates to a larger model, or abstains is usually justified by a confidence signal. Three claims about such a signal do not follow from one another: it ranks answers (discrimination), it supports withholding some of them (selective prediction), and it changes an answer for the better (correction utility). We give an exact decomposition of the third into gated recoveries minus gated harms, which bounds whether a comparison can succeed before it is run: a gate that only replaces a proposal can act only where the base policy was already wrong, so the initial error count caps the discordant pairs any correct gate can produce. When that cap falls below the count a paired test needs, the experiment cannot return a positive result for a working mechanism, nor distinguish one from a gate that never fired. We measure all three targets on two model scales and find the bound binds. In a small-model suite a perturbation-agreement verifier reaches within-policy AUROC 0.990 (95% interval [0.95, 1.00]) while every episode outcome matches single-sample decoding at 4.32 times the call count. In a controlled 840-episode study no verifier replaced the proposal on any of the 60 GSM8K decisions, so that comparison tested nothing; the entire GSM8K gain across six controllers is one task, and it is the task whose identical temperature-zero repeats disagreed, making it the one answer the service does not reproduce. On the diagnostic set the gate could reach four errors while the test needed six, so even a perfect gate had no significant result available. We report two checks that would have caught this before any budget was spent, and show that tie handling in rankings, tied selection cutoffs, and unequal output limits each move a headline number in the same dataset. The binding constraint on this literature is measurement resolution, not the choice of signal.

papers.title: From Preference Data to Personalization: Tracing Sycophancy in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Sycophancy in large language models is often measured as agreement with the user, yet agreement can be appropriate when the user's claim is valid, their preference is genuine, or their experience warrants acknowledgment. We study sycophancy as inappropriate agreement: validating a claim, preference, or self-assessment when the context calls for correction, qualification, or resistance. We introduce a validity-aware sycophancy grader and SycoDrift, a persona-targeted evaluation set of 3,298 validity-annotated probes with controlled annotations for user openness and stakes. We use this framework to analyze three sources of agreement pressure: human preference data, automated judge specification, and in-context personalization. First, preference for validating responses in human datasets (Chatbot Arena, HH-RLHF, Community Alignment) is weak and concentrated where agreement is often appropriate. Second, in a selected-value, single-model experiment, emphasized judge rubrics produce consistent but modest increases relative to paired suppressed rubrics, demonstrating a plausible mechanism for training-time amplification. Third, in off-policy evaluations across 14 models, inference-time personalization increases inappropriate agreement, with the largest effect from matched user profiles placed directly before the query.

papers.title: Literary Language Mashup: Curating Fictions with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an alternative approach to human evaluation of literary fictions by employing LLMs themselves as evaluators within the GrAImes framework. We apply this methodology to assess human-written and AI-generated microfictions in Spanish, to five PhD professors in literature and sixteen literary enthusiasts, and to short stories in both Spanish and English. By comparing the evaluations performed by LLMs with those of human judges, we examine the degree of alignment and divergence between both perspectives, thereby assessing the feasibility of LLMs as auxiliary literary evaluators. Our analysis focuses on the alignment of responses from LLMs with those of human evaluators, providing insights into the potential of LLMs in literary assessment. The conducted experiments reveal that while LLMs cannot be regarded as substitutes for human judges in the evaluation of literary microfictions and short stories, with a Krippendorff's alpha reliability coefficient less than 0.66, they can serve as a valuable tool that offers an initial perspective on the editorial quality of the texts in question.
