In environments where covariate data is limited, we find evidence that case estimates will improve predictions substantially, but that equipping the neural network with memory only leads to meagre improvements. Although the case estimation process and quality will vary significantly between insurers, we provide a standardised methodology for assessing their value.

papers.title: Study of $CP$ violation in $\Lambda_b^0\rightarrow N^*M$ decays with the final-state rescattering mechanism
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the charmless nonleptonic two-body $\Lambda_b$ decays within the framework of final-state rescattering mechanism. Using this framework, we evaluate the relevant hadronic triangle diagrams by performing the loop integrations, retaining both their absorptive and dispersive parts. Based on the established formalism, we analyze the $\Lambda_b \to N^*(1535,1520)M$ decay processes with $M =K_S, K^*_0(700)$, $f_0(500,980), \rho(770), \bar{K}^{*0}$, $\phi$, and predict various physical observables, such as their branching ratios, direct and partial-wave $CP$ asymmetries, as well as decay asymmetry parameters. These two-body decay processes are expected to contribute primarily to the subsequent four-body decay channels, such as $\Lambda_b^0 \to p\,\pi^-\,\pi^+\,\pi^-$, whose $CP$ asymmetry measurements will be accessible at the LHCb experiment.

papers.title: Grundy Values of Node-Kayles on Level-Regular Trees
papers.abstract: Node-Kayles is an impartial combinatorial game played on graphs, in which the two players alternately select a vertex and remove it together with all of its neighbours. By the Sprague--Grundy theorem, every position has a Grundy value that determines its outcome under optimal play. In this paper we study the Grundy values of Node-Kayles on level-regular trees $\T{a}$, $a=(a_1,\dots,a_d)$, in which every vertex at level $i-1$ has exactly $a_i$ children. We determine the Grundy values of all level-regular trees of depth at most two, show that $\G(\T{a})\le d+1$, and prove that $\G(\T{a})>0$ whenever $a_1a_2a_3$ is even, using an explicit mirror strategy. We prove a Leaf-Pair Lemma, which shows that the last branching parameter $a_d$ matters only through its parity, and a Twin Lemma for subgraphs that come in isomorphic pairs; as a consequence, $\G(\T{1,2k,s})=1$ for every $k\ge1$ and every finite sequence $s$. For trees containing a long run of ones, we give a general periodicity criterion: if the Grundy values of a tree with a pendant path of length $h$ are $34$-periodic on a finite window, then they are $34$-periodic for all larger $h$. This criterion extends to paths joining two fixed subtrees, and it explains the eventual periodicity of the families $\T{1^k,2}$ and $\T{2,1^k,2}$. We also show that, in this setting, eventual periodicity is equivalent to the boundedness of the Grundy values. Finally, supported by computations, we conjecture that the Grundy values are eventually periodic, with period $2$, in each branching parameter, and eventually periodic in the length of every run of ones.

papers.title: Micro-Macro Tensor Neural Surrogates for Uncertainty Quantification in Collisional Plasma
papers.abstract: Plasma kinetic equations exhibit pronounced sensitivity to microscopic perturbations in model parameters and data, making reliable and efficient uncertainty quantification (UQ) essential for predictive simulations. However, the cost of uncertainty sampling, the high-dimensional phase space, and multiscale stiffness pose severe challenges to both computational efficiency and error control in traditional numerical methods. These aspects are further emphasized in presence of collisions where the high-dimensional nonlocal collision integrations and conservation properties pose severe constraints. To overcome this, we present a variance-reduced Monte Carlo framework for UQ in the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau (VPL) system, in which neural network surrogates replace the multiple costly evaluations of the Landau collision term. The method couples a high-fidelity, asymptotic-preserving VPL solver with inexpensive, strongly correlated surrogates based on the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Euler--Poisson (EP) equations. For the surrogate models, we introduce a generalization of the separable physics-informed neural network (SPINN), developing a class of tensor neural networks based on an anisotropic micro-macro decomposition, to reduce velocity-moment costs, model complexity, and the curse of dimensionality. To further increase correlation with VPL, we calibrate the VPFP model and design an asymptotic-preserving SPINN whose small- and large-Knudsen limits recover the EP and VP systems, respectively. Numerical experiments show substantial variance reduction over standard Monte Carlo, accurate statistics with far fewer high-fidelity samples, and lower wall-clock time, while maintaining robustness to stochastic dimension.

papers.title: Polynomiality ideals, with applications to polynomial functors over free nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a unital commutative ring. For a monoidal category $C$ whose unit is a zero object, we introduce a descending filtration of the k-linearization of $C$ by two-sided ideals, called the polynomiality ideals: the $d$-th ideal encodes polynomiality of degree at most $d$ for functors from $C$ to $k$-modules. These ideals yield general criteria for the existence of polynomial functors of a given degree and for equivalences between the categories of polynomial functors of degree at most $d$ over different base categories. For Lawvere theories satisfying a mild condition, we identify the polynomiality ideals with powers of augmentation ideals of monoids; this identification makes the criteria computable by means of classical group ring theory. As the main application, we study polynomial functors over finitely generated free nilpotent groups, comparing them across nilpotency classes and polynomial degrees. We obtain refinements of results of Baues and Pirashvili in the case of class at most 2, recover several folklore results for free groups and free abelian groups, and establish a modular analogue formulated with dimension subgroups over a field of positive characteristic in place of the lower central series. Finally, we show that, in contrast to polynomial functors, analytic functors admit no analogous ideal in most cases.

papers.title: Prospect for measurement of CP-violating parameters of $B_s^0 \to \phi\gamma$ at the Tera Z factory
papers.abstract: $b \to s\gamma$ transition is a critical flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) process that could be used to probe CP violation (CPV) and new physics (NP). We quantify the anticipated precision for measuring $B_s^0 \to \phi\gamma$ at the CEPC Z pole operation, showing that the relative statistical uncertainty could be as low as 0.16\%, improved by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to existing measurements. Additionally, we perform a time-dependent analysis of the $B_s^0 \to \phi\gamma$ decay, accounting for $B_s^0/\bar{B}_s^0$ mixing extract the mixing-induced and CP-violating parameters $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}_{\phi\gamma}^\Delta}$, $\boldsymbol{C_{\phi\gamma}}$ and $\boldsymbol{S_{\phi\gamma}}$. Using central value from LHCb measurement as input, we evaluate the anticipated accuracy of measurements of these parameters. The projected statistical uncertainties are $\sigma_{A_{\phi\gamma}^{\Delta}{}^{\text{stat}}} = 0.021$, $\sigma_C^{\text{stat}} = 0.0092$ and $\sigma_S^{\text{stat}} = 0.0096$, and the systematic uncertainties are $\sigma_{A_{\phi\gamma}^{\Delta}{}^{\text{syst}}} = 0.035$, $\sigma_C^{\text{syst}} = 0.0027$ and $\sigma_S^{\text{syst}} = 0.0064$. Furthermore, the 1$\sigma$ sensitivity boundaries for NP in this study are found to be $\mathcal{A}_{\phi\gamma}^\Delta 0.15$, $\mathcal{C}_{\phi\gamma} 0.04$, and $\mathcal{S}_{\phi\gamma} 0.04$. We also conduct a relevant detector optimization study by establishing the correlation between the anticipated precision and the intrinsic resolution of the ECAL, as well as the performance of the PID system.

papers.title: Substrate Role in Polaron Formation on Single-layer Transition Metal Dihalides
papers.abstract: Single-layer transition metal dihalides grown on conducting substrates were shown to host stable polarons. Here, we investigate small polarons in a single layer of the insulator MnBr$_2$, which was grown by molecular beam epitaxy on three different substrates: graphene on Ir(110), graphene on Ir(111), and Au(111). Polarons on these substrates can be created, converted, and moved by the STM tip when a tunneling current flows at a proper bias voltage. Four polaron species are observed in MnBr$_2$ grown on graphene Ir(110), three of which resemble the species previously observed for CoCl$_2$ on graphite, whereas MnBr$_2$ grown on the other substrates exhibits only two of these four species. Changing the substrate from graphene on Ir to Au(111) increases polaron number density by an order of magnitude. These large differences demonstrate that the choice of conducting substrate plays a decisive role in determining polaron phenomenology in substrate-supported single-layer insulators. Two unique observations are reported for polarons in MnBr$_2$ on graphene supported by Ir(110): First, mobile polarons are guided by the periodic potential originating from the super-moir\'e of MnBr$_2$ with graphene and Ir(110); second, polarons remain stable up to 300\,K.

papers.title: Learning Generalizable Hand-Object Tracking from Synthetic Demonstrations
papers.abstract: We present a system for learning generalizable hand-object tracking controllers purely from synthetic data, without requiring any human demonstrations. Our approach makes two key contributions: (1) HOG, a highly efficient Hand-Object data generator that rapidly synthesizes diverse, large-scale, and uniformly distributed trajectories; and (2) HOT, a Hand-Object Tracker that bridges synthetic-to-physical transfer through reinforcement learning and interaction imitation learning. Our method extends to diverse object shapes and hand morphologies. HOT also enables cross-simulator transfer. Through extensive evaluations, we show that our approach enables dexterous hands to track challenging, long-horizon sequences including object re-arrangement and agile in-hand reorientation. These results represent a significant step toward scalable foundation controllers for manipulation that can learn entirely from simple, scalable synthetic data, breaking the data bottleneck that has long constrained progress in dexterous manipulation.

papers.title: CORE: Concept-Oriented Reinforcement for Bridging the Definition-Application Gap in Mathematical Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often solve challenging math exercises yet fail to apply the concept right when the problem requires genuine understanding. Popular Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) pipelines reinforce final answers but provide little fine-grained conceptual signal, so models improve at pattern reuse rather than conceptual applications. We introduce CORE (Concept-Oriented REinforcement), an RL training framework that turns explicit concepts into a controllable supervision signal. Starting from a high-quality, low-contamination textbook resource that links verifiable exercises to concise concept descriptions, we run a sanity probe showing LLMs can restate definitions but fail concept-linked quizzes, quantifying the conceptual reasoning gap. CORE then (i) synthesizes concept-aligned quizzes, (ii) injects brief concept snippets during rollouts to elicit concept-primed trajectories, and (iii) reinforces conceptual reasoning via trajectory replacement after group failures, a lightweight forward-KL constraint that aligns unguided with concept-primed policies, or standard GRPO directly on concept-aligned quizzes. Across several models, CORE delivers consistent gains over vanilla and SFT baselines on both in-domain concept-exercise suites and diverse out-of-domain math benchmarks. CORE unifies direct training on concept-aligned quizzes and concept-injected rollouts under outcome regularization. It provides fine-grained conceptual supervision that bridges problem-solving competence and genuine conceptual reasoning, while remaining algorithm- and verifier-agnostic.

papers.title: Frequentist forecasting in regime-switching models with extended Hamilton filter
papers.abstract: Psychological change processes, such as university student dropout in math, often exhibit discrete latent state transitions and can be studied using regime-switching models with intensive longitudinal data (ILD). Recently, regime-switching state-space (RSSS) models have been extended to allow for latent variables and their autoregressive effects. Despite this progress, there is a need for frequentist estimation methods in dynamic latent variable frameworks that handle both intra-individual changes and inter-individual differences as predictors of regime-switches and allow real-time inferences and forecasts during ongoing data collection. Building on Chow and Zhang's (2013) extended Kim filter, we introduce a first frequentist filter for RSSS models which allows hidden Markov(-switching) models to depend on both latent within- and between-individual characteristics. As a counterpart of Kelava et al.'s (2022) Bayesian forecasting filter for nonlinear dynamic latent class structural equation models (NDLC-SEM), our method is the first frequentist approach within this general class of models. In an empirical study, the filter is applied to forecast emotions and behavior related to student dropout in math. A simulation study shows that marginalizing person-specific random intercepts within the filter cleanly separates autoregressive persistence from stable between-person differences, with accurate out-of-sample regime forecasts, while within-person transition effects stay weakly identified.

papers.title: Toward AI epidemiology: a measurement standardization framework for prospective risk detection
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a measurement standardization framework that compresses expert-AI interactions into structured, comparable fields for prospective risk detection in deployed AI systems, without access to model internals. This concept paper defines the framework's scope, semantically and statistically, and specifies a protocol for its empirical testing. The population-level claims it is designed to support therefore belong to a staged research program rather than to results claimed here. Measurement standardization underpins three claims. The first is a reliability claim: under bounded conditions, large language models can produce reliable, standardized assessments of the evidential and policy alignment of expert-AI interactions. The second is a governance claim: alignment scores give experts an immediate signal during deployment and give institutions a basis for monitoring alignment patterns across mission types, models, and domains. The third is an outcome validation claim: once measurement standardization is established, aggregate alignment scores could be used to study associations with downstream outcomes in regulated professional settings. This introduces the possibility of an "AI epidemiology", a form of risk detection based on correlated variables instead of mechanistic analysis, inspired by epidemiological reasoning. A minimal application of the protocol to a published expert-AI corpus shows that the judge reproduces its policy and evidential alignment scores across two runs under the specified conditions. Judge reliability at scale remains to be validated in future work. The paper sets out a defined grammar of eight interaction fields, together with a statistical protocol based on paired bootstrap inference, DeLong's test for paired AUCs as a sensitivity check, a pre-specified one-sided non-inferiority margin of 0.05, and Holm-Bonferroni correction.

papers.title: Fractional quantization in gapless flat bands with ill-defined topology and divergent quantum geometry
papers.abstract: Fractional quantum anomalous Hall (FQAH) effect, a zero-magnetic-field lattice analog of the fractional quantum Hall effect, offers a unique pathway toward fault-tolerant quantum computation and deep insights into the interplay of topology and strong correlations. The exploration has been successfully guided by the paradigm of ideal flat Chern bands, which mimic Landau levels in both band topology and local quantum geometry. Yet, given the boundless potential for Bloch bands in lattice systems, it remains a significant open question whether FQAH states can arise in scenarios fundamentally distinct from this paradigm. Here we turn to a class of gapless flat bands, featuring (i) ill-defined band topology, (ii) non-quantized Berry flux, (iii) divergent quantum geometry at singular band touchings, (iv) highly fluctuating and far-from-ideal quantum geometry across the Brillouin zone. Our exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group calculations unambiguously demonstrate an FQAH phase that is virtually independent of the interaction strength, persisting from the weak-interaction to the strong-interaction limit. We find the stability of the FQAH states does not uniquely correlate with the singularity strength. Instead, the many-body topological order can adapt to the singular and fluctuating quantum geometric landscape by spontaneously developing an inhomogeneous carrier distribution, while its quenching is accompanied by a drop in the occupation-weighted Berry flux. Our work reveals a profound interplay between local quantum geometry and many-body correlation, and significantly expands the exploration space for the FQAH effect and correlated phenomena in general.

papers.title: Composition laws for homogeneous energies and symphonic maps
papers.abstract: For a spectral energy homogeneous of degree $q>1$ in the differential, we characterize the smooth maps which pull back stationary maps into every Riemannian target. If the scalar density is nonzero, these maps are precisely the $q$-harmonic morphisms. The weak statement requires only $C^1$ regularity in the differential variable. It also covers densities which vanish on the identity of the intermediate tangent space. For the energies of the stress tensor $S$ and its trace-free analogue $T$, the source dimension enters the flux. In dimensions at least two we obtain a complete dichotomy: in equal dimensions the preserving maps are the $2p$-harmonic morphisms, and in unequal dimensions only locally constant maps preserve all targets. A hypersurface of dimension $n$ in a target of dimension $n+1$ detects the obstruction when the source dimension exceeds the intermediate dimension $n$.

papers.title: AutoMV: An Automatic Multi-Agent System for Music Video Generation
papers.abstract: Turning a full song into a music video (MV) requires interpreting its lyrics, which are often metaphorical, multilingual, and repeated across choruses, together with its musical character, and laying the resulting imagery out along the song's structure. Existing music-to-video systems produce short clips or audio-reactive visuals and make little use of lyric meaning. We present AutoMV, a training-free multi-agent framework in which LLM Screenwriter and Director agents plan a full-song visual narrative from time-aligned lyrics and music analysis, keep characters consistent through a shared character bank, and route each shot to cinematic or lip-sync rendering with verification. To evaluate full-song MVs, we build M2VBench: 30 released songs paired with their official MVs, objective audio--visual metrics, and a 12-criterion rubric rated by music-industry experts. Expert evaluation shows that AutoMV outperforms other baselines, although a gap remains to human-produced MVs. Ablation studies highlight the importance of time-aligned lyrics for musical theme alignment and storytelling. We further find that the selected multimodal judge, guided by our evaluation rubric, recovers the expert ranking of automatic systems, with some discrepancies in fine-grained assessments.

papers.title: AGN x-ray reflection spectroscopy with ML_MYTORUS: Neural posterior estimation with training on observation-driven parameter grids
papers.abstract: X-ray spectroscopy of active galactic nuclei (AGN) probes circumnuclear matter geometry. Many AGN show a narrow Fe K $\alpha$ line at 6.4 keV and associated Compton-scattered continua in their x-ray spectra, due to primary continuum scattering in cold, neutral material far from the central supermassive black hole. We present a novel approach via Simulation-Based Inference with Neural Posterior Estimation (SBI-NPE) and train a machine learning neural network (ML NN) model based on $NuSTAR$ spectral fitting results from the literature, employing the physically motivated MYTORUS-decoupled model, which distinguishes line-of-sight from global equivalent neutral hydrogen column density ($N_{\rm H,Z}$ vs. $N_{\rm H,S}$). To overcome the limitations of traditional frequentist fitting (e.g., lack of automation, reproducibility, computational cost), we implement normalizing flows and autoregressive networks to learn flexible posterior distributions from simulated spectra. From 34 $NuSTAR$ spectral fitting literature results, we simulate 34,000 spectra for both a uniform and a Gaussian parameter distribution. We train our neural network to determine four key MYTORUS parameters, $N_{H,Z}, N_{H,S}$, power-law spectral index $\Gamma$, and relative normalization $A_{\rm S}$. The observation-based grid significantly outperforms uniform sampling, achieving predictive accuracy for individual parameters >90% ($N_{H,S}$ and $A_{\rm S}$), 89% ($N_{\rm H,Z}$), and 82% ($\Gamma$) within $\pm1\sigma$. For all four parameters simultaneously, predictive accuracy remains high ($\sim$70%). The trained NN ML, ML_MYTORUS, is publicly available with a web interface for fast and reproducible parameter inference from $NuSTAR$ spectra. We illustrate its use via application to NGC 4388. This work shows that SBI offers great potential for future distant x-ray reflection studies in AGN or Galactic x-ray binary spectra.

papers.title: Modular Witten Diagrams and Quantum Extremality
papers.abstract: We study entanglement entropy for ball-shaped regions in excited states of holographic conformal field theories. The excited states are prepared by the Euclidean path integral in the CFT with a source turned on for some double-trace operator, with a small, $O(1)$ amplitude $\lambda$. On the gravity side, the double-trace operator deforms the bulk geometry as well as the entanglement structure of the state of bulk matter fields. By the quantum extremal surface formula, this leads to a deformation of the shape of the entanglement wedge, an effect which becomes manifest in the entanglement entropy at $O(\lambda^2 G_N)$. On the CFT side, we explicitly calculate the entanglement entropy perturbatively in the source amplitude to $O(\lambda^2)$, in terms of modular-flowed correlation functions of double-trace operators. We then evaluate these modular-flowed correlation functions using Witten diagrams. This calculation involves a Schwinger-Keldysh contour ordering prescription in the bulk, which we motivate using analytic continuation from Euclidean replica correlators. Focusing on a particular graviton-exchange diagram, we rewrite it in a form where it manifestly reproduces the canonical energy term present in the quantum Ryu-Takayanagi formula, including the shape deformation of the entanglement wedge due to backreaction and quantum effects.

papers.title: Asymptotic statistics for finite continued fractions with restricted digits
papers.abstract: Zaremba's conjecture concerns a formation of continued fraction expansions for rational numbers with partial quotient bounded by an absolute constant. We present asymptotic estimates for the size of $\epsilon$-thickening of certain fractal sets of bounded-type, which in turn provide a remark on Zaremba's conjecture in an averaging sense. We also discuss a generalisation for complex continued fractions over imaginary quadratic fields.

papers.title: Integrated Generation and Purification of Entangled Coherent States for Non-Gaussian Teleportation
papers.abstract: Entangled coherent states (ECS) provide a powerful non-Gaussian resource for continuous-variable (CV) quantum communication, but their generation in scalable architectures remains challenging. We propose an integrated photonic scheme that creates high-fidelity quasi-entangled coherent states (quasi-ECS) from a two-mode squeezed vacuum state (TMSVS) via photon subtraction in a symmetric waveguide trimer. The resulting non-Gaussian entanglement is further enhanced by single-photon catalysis, which purifies the distributed state after transmission through lossy channels. The improvement in conditional teleportation fidelity is accompanied by a reduced heralding probability. Using these purified quasi-ECS resources, we analyze a photon-number-based teleportation protocol and demonstrate high-fidelity transfer of both coherent states and Schrodinger cat states. For the logical cat qubit, we use an orthogonal even/odd-cat basis, measurement-dependent phase corrections, and the success-probability-weighted fidelity over six logical input states. For completeness and benchmarking, we also study the Braunstein-Kimble (BK) teleportation protocol using Gaussian TMSVSs. In particular, the teleportation fidelity for cat states exceeds the benchmark value of 2/3 over a broad range of realistic channel and squeezing parameters. By contrast, the underlying TMSVS performs poorly within the photon-number-based protocol, whereas in the BK protocol it exceeds this benchmark only in a restricted regime of high squeezing and high transmissivity. Our results show that integrated photon subtraction and catalysis enable practical, chip-compatible generation of non-Gaussian entanglement suitable for advanced quantum teleportation and CV quantum networks.

papers.title: A Taxonomy of Numerical Differentiation Methods
papers.abstract: Differentiation is a cornerstone of computing and data analysis in every discipline of science and engineering. Indeed, most fundamental physics laws are expressed as relationships between derivatives in space and time. However, derivatives are rarely directly measurable and must instead be computed, often from noisy, potentially corrupt data streams. There is a rich and broad literature of computational differentiation algorithms, but many impose extra constraints to work correctly, e.g. periodic boundary conditions, or are compromised in the presence of noise and corruption. It can therefore be challenging to select the method best-suited to any particular problem. Here we review a broad range of numerical methods for calculating derivatives, present important contextual considerations and choice points, compare relative advantages, and provide basic theory for each algorithm in order to assist users with the mathematical underpinnings. This serves as a practical guide to help scientists and engineers match methods to application domains. We also provide an open-source Python package, PyNumDiff, which contains a broad suite of methods for differentiating noisy data.

papers.title: Blown-up singular Riemannian foliations
papers.abstract: We study the effect of projective blow-ups on the leaf closures and basic cohomology of singular Riemannian foliations. For a foliation with smooth Molino sheaf on a compact manifold, we show that the Molino sheaf of the blow-up is the inverse image of the original sheaf under blow-down. In particular, desingularization preserves the Killing property and the structural Lie algebra. We obtain a closedness criterion in terms of the Euler characteristics of the ambient manifold and the blow-up centers, assuming finite fundamental group and singular strata of codimension at least three. For singular Killing foliations on compact manifolds, we approximate the space of leaf closures in Gromov--Hausdorff distance by Riemannian orbifolds whose dimension equals the codimension of the foliation. Finally, relative basic cohomology gives a long exact sequence relating the original foliation, its blow-up, and their restrictions to the center and the exceptional divisor.

papers.title: Seaweed algebras with restricted part sizes
papers.abstract: Seaweed algebras are a class of Lie algebras that are naturally characterized by a pair of compositions, which in turn are represented visually as planar graphs called meanders. These meanders provide a straightforward method for computing the index of the associated algebra. The goal of this paper is to enumerate those seaweed algebras with a fixed index and whose associated compositions have restricted part sizes. In particular, we enumerate those with composition part sizes from so-called acyclic sets. We also establish a bijection between sets of indecomposable seaweed algebras with meanders with certain restricted part sizes and sets of permutations with restricted displacements. In certain cases, the index of the algebra can be determined by a simple statistic on the permutation.

papers.title: Intra-Agent Motion and Inter-Agent Relation Learning for Map-Free Trajectory Prediction
papers.abstract: Trajectory prediction is essential for safe planning and decision-making in autonomous driving. Map-free prediction improves deployment flexibility by removing the dependence on high-definition maps, but it also loses explicit road-topology and lane-connectivity priors. Consequently, the model must recover stable motion cues from short histories while resolving prospective interaction relations without lane-level guidance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a map-free trajectory prediction framework centered on a novel Goal-Conditioned Expert-Routed Transformer (GCERT). A lightweight intra-agent front-end first decomposes projected historical motion features into a smooth trend and a local detail residual through a centered moving average. Component-specific residual projections transform the two signals before a causal temporal Transformer summarizes their recombined evolution. GCERT employs dual-level expert routing: edge-level relation experts generate interaction-specific messages, while node-level state experts adapt the transformation after message aggregation. Predicted motion goals update the node representations and construct prospective relative-geometry and orientation edge features before the final interaction layer, thereby conditioning attention, relation-specific message generation, and state transformation. GCERT therefore determines not only which neighboring agents should be attended to, but also what relation-specific information should be transmitted and how the aggregated node state should be transformed. The resulting representations are decoded into multimodal future trajectories and jointly optimized with trajectory-regression, mode-classification, and goal-prediction objectives.

papers.title: Generalized Boltzmann-Gibbs Distributions and the Electronic Partition Function Paradox
papers.abstract: The maximization of the nonadditive entropic functional $S_{q}(p)=k\sum_{i}p_{i}\ln_{q}(1/p_{i})$, $q\in(0,1)$, under a linear mean-energy constraint, i.e., the best-behaved case from Dognini and Tsallis (2026), is used to derive generalizations of the Boltzmann-Gibbs distribution for physical systems whose description requires a limiting process over the energy spectrum: the hydrogen atom in free space; an energy spectrum that uniformly approaches a continuous, unbounded limit with a common degeneracy; the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of velocities; the harmonic oscillator; and the one-dimensional box. For the hydrogen atom with mean energy $U\in[0,e_{ion}]$, the limiting optimal distribution is a two-tier one, concentrated on the ground level and on the ionization threshold, with weights $1-U/e_{ion}$ and $U/e_{ion}$ for every $q\in(0,1)$, and the temperature rescaled by $\ln_{q}W$ is finite and given by $T_{q,s}=T_{ion}(U/e_{ion})^{1-q}$, with $T_{ion}=e_{ion}/kq$. This circumvents the Electronic Partition Function Paradox and yields a family of well-defined thermodynamic behaviors.

papers.title: Functional Compression as Occam's Razor: Algebraic Complexity from Sensitivity Minimization
papers.abstract: Discovering discrete algebraic structures from data is a fundamental challenge in machine learning. We ask how continuous learning objectives can favor functional compression---representing data through shared algebraic composition rather than low-rank representations. We analyze the global optima of a canonical factorization model for algebraic completion (recovering finite binary operations) that demonstrated a preference for group operations. We measure algebraic complexity by the infimum of parameter sensitivity under exact reconstruction. We establish a universal complexity floor, whose attainment forces geometric alignment and unitarity of the latent representations. At the floor, input representations compose into the corresponding output representations; their reuse across the operation table propagates these local identities to enforce a globally shared algebraic structure. If the floor is not attained, a positive gap separates it from the feasible infimum. For cancellative operations, floor attainment forces the model's latent representation to be an injective homomorphism, equivalent to the target being isotopic to a group. In this case, every global minimizer is equivalent to the underlying group's unitary left-regular representation, up to isotopy and unitary gauge, resolving the central conjecture of Huh (2025). For non-cancellative operations, floor attainment forces exact structural redundancies (identical rows or columns) and is equivalent to a unitary factorization of the target's row- and column-reduced table with orthonormal output matrices, yielding the fewest distinct input matrices compatible with exact reconstruction. The resulting cancellative table then embeds in a group-isotope table. This analysis reveals a structural bias toward functional compression: at the sensitivity floor, algebraic composition of latent representations implements the target operation.

papers.title: Improved parameter initialization for the (local) unitary cluster Jastrow ansatz
papers.abstract: The unitary cluster Jastrow (UCJ) ansatz and its variant known as local UCJ (LUCJ) are promising choices for variational quantum algorithms for chemistry due to their combination of physical motivation and hardware efficiency. The parameters of these ansatzes can be initialized from the output of a coupled cluster, singles and doubles (CCSD) calculation performed on a classical computer. However, truncating the number of repetitions of the ansatz, as well as discarding interactions to accommodate the connectivity constraints of near-term quantum processors, degrade the approximation to CCSD and the resulting energy accuracy. In this work, we propose two methods to improve the parameter initialization. The first method, which is applicable to both expectation value- and sample-based algorithms, uses compressed double factorization of the CCSD amplitudes to improve or recover the CCSD approximation. The second method, which is applicable to sample-based algorithms, uses approximate tensor network simulation to improve the quality of samples produced by the ansatz circuit. Both methods perform classical preprocessing to construct the initial circuit parameters and can be followed by parameter optimization using quantum measurements, although we do not perform such optimization in this work. We validate our methods using exact state vector simulation on systems of up to 52 qubits, as well as experiments on superconducting quantum processors using up to 65 qubits. Our results indicate that our methods can significantly improve the output of both expectation value- and sample-based quantum algorithms.

papers.title: On the $2$-torsion in class groups of number fields
papers.abstract: In $2020$, Bhargava, Shankar, Taniguchi, Thorne, Tsimerman, and Zhao proved that for a finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}$ of degree $n\geq 5$, the size of the $2$-torsion class group is bounded by $\# h_{2}(K)=O_{n,\varepsilon}(D_{K}^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2n}+\varepsilon})$, where $D_{K}$ is the absolute discriminant of $K$. In the present paper, we improve their bound by proving that $\# h_{2}(K)=O_{n,\varepsilon}(D_{K}^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2n}-\delta_{K}+\varepsilon})$, for a constant $\delta_{K}\geq\frac{1}{28n}-\frac{3}{28n(n-1)}$.

papers.title: From Strategy Search to Policy Learning: MCTS-Guided Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Safety Alignment
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly power web-facing applications, including conversational assistants and content services, where open user interaction exposes them to diverse safety threats and adaptive attacks. In particular, jailbreak attackers repeatedly reformulate harmful requests to bypass safety alignment. Although existing studies have concentrated on defending dynamic jailbreaks, they often retain discovered attacks as flat samples and discard information about how those attacks were found. In this paper, we introduce MACE, an MCTS-guided adversarial co-evolution framework that turns search into policy-learning signals for both an attacker and a defender. Its search component, GS-MCTS, explores multi-step compositions of rewriting operators and associates discovered attacks with empirical success frequency and path depth. Its optimization component, AC-TGPO, uses these statistics for difficulty-aware group-relative credit assignment and constructs a temporally asymmetric curriculum from current interactions, pairings between the latest attacker and preceding defender, and attacks that survive a defense update. Thus, MACE connects search structure to both within-round policy optimization and cross-round memory, rather than using MCTS only to generate attacks or treating each round as a flat adversarial dataset. Removing difficulty-aware weighting, asymmetric samples, or persistent hard samples increases defense ASR-LR by 3.7 %, 6.0 %, and 5.0 %, respectively. Across evaluated models, the resulting attacker achieves the highest ASR-LR in all six model--dataset settings, while the defender reduces average ASR-LR from 11.9 % for the best baseline to 8.8 %.

papers.title: A physics-constrained neural solver for incompressible flows without labeled data
papers.abstract: We present a physics-constrained neural solver for incompressible flow that requires neither labeled data nor supervised pretraining. The solver enforces incompressibility and boundary conditions (BCs) to strict tolerances. We attribute the limited Reynolds numbers of existing physics-informed approaches to insufficient enforcement of these constraints, on which conventional finite-difference and finite-volume solvers depend. We therefore formulate incompressible flow as a constrained optimization problem within the physics- and equality-constrained artificial neural network (PECANN) framework: the pressure Poisson residual is minimized subject to the momentum equations, continuity equation, and BCs imposed as equality constraints on the primitive variables, while a conditionally adaptive augmented Lagrangian method enforces each constraint. The pressure Poisson objective proves critical. Across all benchmarks, replacing it with the momentum residual fails to converge to accurate solutions under identical architecture and constraint enforcement, which we attribute to the global elliptic coupling of pressure and velocity that local momentum-residual minimization lacks. For advection-dominated flows, we introduce an adaptive vanishing entropy viscosity that stabilizes training while leaving the converged solution unchanged. The solver predicts lid-driven cavity flow up to Re = 7,500 with centerline velocity profiles matching benchmark data, and is further validated on flow over a backward-facing step at Re = 800, 3D unsteady Beltrami flow, and steady and unsteady flow past a circular cylinder under an inflow-outflow configuration, for which an ablation study identifies admissible outlet BCs for velocity and pressure. From a randomly initialized network and without external perturbations, the solver captures the spontaneous onset of periodic vortex shedding in unsteady cylinder flow.

papers.title: BPS Solutions of 4d Euclidean N=2 Supergravity with Higher Derivative Interactions
papers.abstract: We study fully BPS and a broad class of half-BPS stationary configurations of four-dimensional Euclidean N=2 supergravity with higher-derivative interactions. Working within the off-shell conformal supergravity framework of de Wit and Reys (arXiv:1706.04973), we analyse the complete set of Killing spinor equations and obtain the corresponding algebraic and differential constraints. We further derive the Euclidean attractor equations and evaluate the Wald entropy for the fully BPS AdS_2 x S^2 background. For half-BPS stationary configurations, we obtain the generalized stabilization equations expressing all fields in terms of harmonic functions on three-dimensional flat base space, extending the Lorentzian analysis of Cardoso et al (arXiv:hep-th/0009234) to the Euclidean signature. Our results provide a framework for studying supersymmetric saddles and computing the gravitational indices entirely within Euclidean higher-derivative supergravity, without recourse to analytic continuation.

papers.title: Delay-Aware Distributed Multi-Robot Motion Planning
papers.abstract: This paper examines why distributed optimization degrades when multi-robot systems coordinate under realistic communication delays. Using consensus ADMM as a representative framework for generating collision-free, dynamically feasible motion plans in both trajectory optimization and receding-horizon control settings, we show that delay degrades performance structurally: the consensus and dual updates weight stale and current information identically, so staleness enters the optimizer disguised as genuine disagreement and accumulates through the multipliers. Delay-agnostic adaptation (e.g. residual balancing) inherits this contamination and can perform worse than a fixed penalty. We introduce a Delay-Aware ADMM (DA-ADMM) variant that adapts penalty parameters to real-time delay statistics and re-derives the global consensus update as a delay-weighted average, down-weighting stale information in favor of recent updates. Simulations in 2D and 3D show that DA-ADMM improves robustness, success rate, and solution quality over fixed-parameter, residual-balancing, lower-bound, and fixed-constraint baselines. Degradation is therefore governed not by delay length or frequency, but by the optimizer's ability to reason over the age of the information it receives.

papers.title: Notes on Stack Machines and Quantum Stack Machines
papers.abstract: Multi-stack machines and Turing machines can simulate to each other. In this note, we give a succinct definition of multi-stack machines, and from this definition it is clearly seen that pushdown automata and deterministic finite automata are special cases of multi-stack machines. Also, with this mode of definition, pushdown automata and deterministic pushdown automata are equivalent and recognize all context-free languages. In addition, we are motivated to formulate concise definitions of quantum pushdown automata and quantum stack machines.

papers.title: PSM: Prompt Sensitivity Minimization via LLM-Guided Black-Box Optimization
papers.abstract: System prompts are critical for guiding the behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet they often contain proprietary logic or sensitive information, making them a prime target for extraction attacks. Adversarial queries can successfully elicit these hidden instructions, posing significant security and privacy risks. Existing defense mechanisms frequently rely on heuristics, incur substantial computational overhead, or are inapplicable to models accessed via black-box APIs. This paper introduces a novel framework for hardening system prompts through shield appending, a lightweight approach that adds a protective textual layer to the original prompt. Our core contribution is the formalization of prompt hardening as a utility-constrained optimization problem. We leverage an LLM-as-optimizer to search the space of possible SHIELDs, seeking to minimize a leakage metric derived from a suite of adversarial attacks, while simultaneously preserving task utility above a specified threshold, measured by semantic fidelity to baseline outputs. This black-box, optimization-driven methodology is lightweight and practical, requiring only API access to the target and optimizer LLMs. We demonstrate empirically that our optimized SHIELDs significantly reduce prompt leakage against a comprehensive set of extraction attacks, outperforming established baseline defenses without compromising the model's intended functionality. Our work presents a paradigm for developing robust, utility-aware defenses in the escalating landscape of LLM security. The code is made public on the following link: https://github.com/psm-defense/psm

papers.title: Coherent high-velocity chiral magnons in the metallic altermagnet CrSb
papers.abstract: Altermagnets combine the zero net magnetization of antiferromagnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting, creating new opportunities for spintronic and magnonic technologies. The full realization of this promise necessitates a material that is simultaneously metallic and altermagnetic, yet preserves the long magnon lifetimes more often seen in insulators. Here, we use polarized neutron diffraction and inelastic neutron scattering to determine the magnetic structure and spin dynamics of the metallic altermagnet CrSb. We confirm a fully compensated, collinear magnetic structure with localized Cr moments and establish the microscopic spin Hamiltonian governing its excitations. Despite its metallicity, CrSb hosts remarkably coherent magnons across its 230 meV bandwidth, with group velocities approaching 60 km/s. Along low-symmetry momentum directions, we resolve chiral magnon splitting generated by higher-order, symmetry-inequivalent exchange interactions, providing the first experimental observation of this phenomenon in a metallic altermagnet. These results reveal a nearly complete separation between magnetic and electronic degrees of freedom in CrSb and demonstrate that metallic transport, room-temperature altermagnetic order, fast coherent magnons, and chiral spin dynamics can coexist in a single material, positioning CrSb as a compelling platform for spintronic applications.

papers.title: SURFing to the Fundamental Limit of Jet Tagging
papers.abstract: Beyond the practical goal of improving search and measurement sensitivity through better jet tagging algorithms, there is a deeper question: what are their upper performance limits? Generative surrogate models with learned likelihood functions offer a new approach to this problem, provided the surrogate correctly captures the underlying data distribution. In this work, we introduce the SUrrogate ReFerence (SURF) method, a new approach to validating generative models. This framework enables exact Neyman-Pearson tests by training the target model on samples from another tractable surrogate, which is itself trained on real data. We argue that the EPiC-FM generative model is a valid surrogate reference for JetClass jets and apply SURF to show that modern jet taggers may already be operating close to the true statistical limit. By contrast, we find that autoregressive GPT models unphysically exaggerate top vs. QCD separation power encoded in the surrogate reference, implying that they are giving a misleading picture of the fundamental limit.

papers.title: Keeping It Renormalizable: Minimal Baryogenesis induced Asymmetric Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Many asymmetric dark matter scenarios have been proposed to date. Among them, perhaps the most motivated ones are those in which the dark matter asymmetry is induced from the baryon/lepton asymmetries via chemical equilibration without any new sources of CP violation. However, most of the models put forward along these lines have been excluded by now and/or are based on complicated setups. In this letter, we present a new, simple, and viable scenario. It assumes only two new fields: a scalar singlet and an inert scalar doublet, and is based only on renormalizable interactions, that slowly generate the dark matter asymmetry from the Standard Model Higgs asymmetry. The successful asymmetry transfer requires small (but technically natural) couplings which in turn make the model CP conserving in practice. The model allows for the direct detection of dark matter in the upcoming generation of experiments, and the inert doublet is predicted to be light enough to be potentially produced and observed at the LHC and future colliders, $46\,{\rm GeV}<m_{H'}<580\,{\rm GeV}$. Quite remarkably, the mass and lifetime of the inert doublet may be inferred from direct detection experiments, indicating long-lived compressed electroweak states that can be searched for at the HL-LHC.

papers.title: Control strategies for magnetized plasma: a polar coordinates framework
papers.abstract: In this work, we provide an overview of various control strategies aimed at steering plasma toward desired configurations using an external magnetic field. From a modeling perspective, we focus on the Vlasov equation in a two-dimensional bounded domain, accounting for both a self-induced electric field and a strong external magnetic field. The results are presented in a polar coordinate framework, which is particularly well-suited for simulating toroidal devices such as Tokamaks and Stellarators. A key feature of the proposed control strategies is their feedback mechanism, which is based on an instantaneous prediction of the discretized system. Finally, different numerical experiments in the two-dimensional polar coordinate setting demonstrate the effectiveness of the approaches.

papers.title: A kernel method for the learning of Wasserstein geometric flows
papers.abstract: Wasserstein gradient and Hamiltonian flows provide geometric formulations of many partial differential equations. We develop a structure-preserving kernel method for jointly estimating the external potential and interaction kernel governing these flows, assuming a known internal energy. The inverse problem is formulated through a trajectory-dependent observation operator and regularized in a product of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, yielding an explicit finite representation of the estimator. We characterize joint non-identifiability through the null space of the observation operator and derive a Fourier criterion on the torus, distinguishing uniqueness of the regularized estimator from recovery of the underlying physical components. We establish reconstruction error bounds and convergence rates under source conditions and suitable regularization and mesh refinement, together with a stability estimate for Hamiltonian flows with vanishing internal energy. Numerical experiments demonstrate joint reconstruction and illustrate how unobservable interaction modes can prevent accurate potential recovery despite small observation-equation residuals. A comparison with sparse learning illustrates the dependence of reconstruction accuracy on the chosen dictionary.

papers.title: Efficient and rate-optimal list-decoding in the presence of minimal feedback
papers.abstract: Given a channel with length-$n$ inputs and outputs over the alphabet $\{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}$, and of which a fraction $\varrho \in (0,1-1/q)$ of symbols can be arbitrarily corrupted by an adversary, a fundamental problem is that of communicating at rates close to the information-theoretically optimal values, while ensuring the receiver can infer that the transmitter's message is from a ``small" set. While the existence of such codes is known, and constructions with computationally tractable encoding/decoding procedures are known for large $q$, we provide the first schemes that attain this performance for any $q \geq 2$, as long as low-rate feedback (asymptotically negligible relative to the number of transmissions) from the receiver to the transmitter is available. For any sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ and $\varrho \in (1-{1}/{q}-\Theta(\sqrt{\varepsilon}))$ our minimal feedback scheme has the following parameters: Rate $1-H_q(\varrho) - \varepsilon$ (i.e., $\varepsilon$-close to information-theoretically optimal -- here $H_q(\varrho)$ is the $q$-ary entropy function), list-size $\exp\left(\mathcal{O}\left(\varepsilon^{-3/2}\log^2(1/\varepsilon)\right)\right)$, computational complexity of encoding/decoding $n^{\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1}\log(1/\varepsilon))}$, storage complexity $\mathcal{O}(n^{\eta+1}\log n)$ for a code design parameter $\eta>1$ that trades off storage complexity with the probability of error. The error probability is $\mathcal{O}(n^{-\eta})$, and the (vanishing) feedback rate is $\mathcal{O}({1}/{\sqrt{\log(n)}})$. Our full-feedback scheme has zero probability of error and minimal storage complexity, while the other parameters are the same as the vanishing rate feedback scheme.

papers.title: Lower Bounds on High Moments of Twisted Fourier coefficients of Modular Forms
papers.abstract: For any large prime $q$, $x \leq 1$ and any real $k\geq 2$, we prove a lower bound for the following $2k$-th moment \begin{equation*} \sum_{\substack{\chi \in X_q^*}} \Big| \sum_{n\leq x} \chi(n)\lambda(n)\Big|^{2k}, \end{equation*} where $X_q^*$ denotes the set of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q$ and $\lambda(n)$ the Fourier coefficients of a fixed modular form. The bound we obtain is sharp up to a constant factor under the generalized Riemann Hypothesis.

papers.title: Virasoro elements in conformal algebras
papers.abstract: It is well known that Virasoro elements play an extremely important role in the theory of vertex operator algebras, and likewise a very significant role in the field of conformal algebras. In this paper, we introduce the notion of a regular action in the category of conformal modules over Lie conformal algebras with Virasoro elements. We show that a finite conformal module over the general conformal algebra $\mathfrak{gc}_1$ (resp., $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ with $N\ge2$) is semisimple if and only if there exists a pair of different Virasoro elements (resp., canonical Virasoro elements) with regular actions. Along the way to finding semisimplicity criteria, we also discuss the classification of Virasoro elements of $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ in-depth, leading us to construct a huge number of new Virasoro conformal modules.

papers.title: Non-commutative crepant resolutions of toric singularities with divisor class group of rank one
papers.abstract: We classify the basic reflexive modules giving toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) of Gorenstein toric singularities whose divisor class group has rank one. Their isomorphism classes are parametrized by nonempty proper upper sets in a partially ordered quotient of the class group. Each upper set determines a finite subset called its window, which specifies the divisorial summands. The number of summands in each such module equals the normalized volume of the associated lattice polytope, as conjectured by Van den Bergh. If two upper sets differ by one element, their modules are related by a finite sequence of Iyama--Wemyss mutations. Such sequences connect any two of the classified modules, so all toric NCCRs of a fixed singularity are derived equivalent. We construct higher-dimensional analogues of dimer dual quivers when the associated $d$-dimensional lattice polytope is non-pyramidal. The same window determines a cut of a periodic quiver on the $d$-torus. The cut gives an explicit presentation of the endomorphism algebra by a quiver with relations. For $d=2$, the resulting quiver is dual to a dimer model, a bipartite tiling of the two-torus.

papers.title: Cross-Epoch Bias in SGD-based Leave-One-Out Influence: Analysis and Accumulative Correction
papers.abstract: Training-data influence estimates support data selection and cleansing by predicting the effects of removing individual examples. The standard multi-epoch SGD-Influence Estimator (SGD-IE) aggregates contributions from a sample's repeated appearances along the recorded trajectory. When used to approximate finite deletion, it omits an interaction: later removals act on the parameter displacement accumulated from earlier removals. We introduce the Accumulative SGD-Influence Estimator (ACC-SGD-IE) to account for how earlier removals change the effect of removing the same sample again. It uses the sample's Hessian at subsequent appearances to correct the estimated parameter change. Our non-convex analysis shows that this correction removes SGD-IE's additional interaction contribution from the finite-horizon error bound: the omitted interaction produces a local error linear in the accumulated parameter change, while the remaining Taylor remainder is bounded quadratically under Lipschitz-Hessian assumptions. The bounds characterize how training propagates the remaining error. In non-convex experiments across clean and noisy tabular, text, and vision datasets, ACC-SGD-IE reduces validation-loss-change RMSE by 10.8% and improves Jaccard@10% by 15.2% on average relative to SGD-IE. These gains also translate into lower test misclassification rates after data cleansing on MNIST and CIFAR10 at the evaluated removal budgets. On noisy industrial datasets, it reduces aggregate parameter RMS error with a mean relative reduction of 53.4%. We further discuss computational tradeoffs, provide complementary theoretical analysis and experimental evaluation for strongly convex objectives, and explore potential extensions of the accumulative correction mechanism to other influence estimators.

papers.title: On a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture via categorical representations
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a complex reductive group. For a smooth affine spherical $G$-variety $X$ such that the stabilizer of a point in the $B$-orbit under the $B$-action be connected, assume that the unramified relative local Langlands conjecture of Ben-Zvi-Sakellaridis-Venkatesh (BZSV) for $X$ holds. We establish a spectral description of a full subcategory of Iwahori equivariant coherent D-modules on $LX$ in terms of the relative Langlands dual of $X$, confirming a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture proposed by Devalapurkar.

papers.title: InFeR: Informed Failure Resilience in Learned Visual Navigation Control
papers.abstract: While imitation learning (IL) has enabled successful visual navigation in many common environments, IL policies are prone to unpredictable failures under out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios. This necessitates failure-resilient policies, which not only detect failures, but also recognise their sources and recover from them autonomously. We propose InFeR, a general framework for building IL policies with informed failure resilience without failure or recovery demonstrations. Given an IL policy's architecture and training dataset, InFeR retrains a new OOD-aware policy with a latent space structured for OOD failure detection, with a modified objective based on the Variational Information Bottleneck. It applies a visual explainability technique, Grad-CAM, to attribute failures to specific image regions and inform a heuristic policy for recovery. All these are achieved without requiring additional training data. Real-world experiments show that InFeR enables informed failure recovery across two different policy architectures, supporting long-range navigation in complex environments.

papers.title: PathoGaze1.0: An AI-Ready Navigation, Eye-Tracking, and Decision Dataset in Pathology
papers.abstract: Performing cancer diagnosis on giga-pixel whole-slide images (WSIs) is an important but difficult visual search task. The large giga-pixel image size forces pathologists to navigate by zooming and panning to search tissue for malignancy. Diagnostic accuracy averages around 70%, and adding a second pathologist does not substantially improve consistencies between diagnoses. There is a lack of publicly available behavioral data to explain these diagnostic errors and inconsistencies. To fill this gap, we curated PathoGaze1.0, a comprehensive behavioral dataset capturing high-fidelity clinical diagnostic workflows across 11 different pathologist participants over two experiments 12-months apart (8 overlapping pathologists across both experiments), as they interpreted 397 WSIs from CAMELYON16, a set of publicly available breast cancer lymph node WSIs. The dataset comprises 18.69 hours of eye-tracking (171,909 fixations), and navigational scanning data along with 1,140 diagnostic decisions, all collected using a newly-developed testbed PTAH. The testbed supports interaction techniques found in clinical tools and collects viewport, mouse actions, and diagnostic decisions, enabling cross-links between WSI image stimulus, gaze, navigation behaviors, and diagnostic decisions. We share preregistered experimental materials, the datasets, and processing methods on the Open Science Framework (OSF).

papers.title: Chiral gapped states are universally non-topological
papers.abstract: We propose an operator generalization of the Li-Haldane conjecture regarding the entanglement Hamiltonian of a disk in a 2+1D chiral gapped groundstate. The logic applies to regions with sharp corners, from which we derive several universal properties regarding corner entanglement. These universal properties follow from a set of locally-checkable conditions on the wavefunction. We also define a quantity $(\mathfrak{c}_{\text{tot}})_{\text{min}}$ that reflects the robustness of corner entanglement contributions, and show that it provides an obstruction to a gapped boundary. One reward from our analysis is that we can construct a local gapped Hamiltonian within the same chiral gapped phase from a given wavefunction; we conjecture that it is closer to the low-energy renormalization group fixed point than the original parent Hamiltonian. Our analysis of corner entanglement reveals the emergence of a universal conformal geometry encoded in the entanglement structure of bulk regions of chiral gapped states that is not visible in topological field theory. Our formalism also gives an explanation of the modular commutator formula for the chiral central charge.

papers.title: Electrokinetic effects on flow and ion transport in charge-patterned corrugated nanochannels
papers.abstract: The phase offset between surface charge modulation and geometric undulations in a corrugated nanochannel provides a tunable mechanism for rectified, diode-like ion transport under purely pressure-driven conditions: reversing the applied pressure gradient selectively activates transport of opposite ionic species, generating a net ionic current whose sign and magnitude are set by the charge-geometry alignment. Fully coupled Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Stokes simulations reveal the underlying two-regime structure: at low driving force (Regime I), throughput is suppressed below the Poiseuille limit by a localized streaming potential that pins counterions within the electric double layer; above a threshold pressure (Regime II), the mechanical force overcomes electrostatic resistance, producing an abrupt, orders-of-magnitude rise in mean velocity. Electroosmotically driven flow undergoes a qualitatively similar but smoother transition. Peak charge selectivity is achieved at near-complete electric double layer overlap and driving forces just below the Regime I-Regime II transition. Random walk particle tracking confirms selective rectification and quantifies the dependence of ion dispersion on surface charge placement across both regimes.

papers.title: Harnessing Intrinsic Noise for Quantum Simulation of Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Simulating open quantum systems on quantum computers is challenging because dissipative dynamics are nonunitary, whereas gate-based quantum algorithms are typically built from unitary operations. Conventional approaches can overcome this mismatch by embedding nonunitary processes into enlarged unitary circuits, often with ancillary-qubit and gate overhead. In this work, we propose an alternative perspective in which we selectively preserve the physical noise to emulate nonunitary channels. More specifically, we present a partial encoding algorithm that iteratively leverages intrinsic noise to mimic the dynamics of a target open-system. We benchmark the convergence of this algorithm against the dissipative exciton transport Hamiltonian and retrieve their dynamics. By utilizing intrinsic hardware noise to emulate the target nonunitary dynamics, this approach avoids the dual overhead of error-correcting that noise and using ancillary qubits to re-introduce nonunitarity. This significantly reduces both qubit requirements and physical fidelity thresholds, paving the way for more efficient techniques to simulate open quantum systems on quantum computers.

papers.title: All-Gaussian State Discrimination Beyond the Coherent Helstrom Bound
papers.abstract: A core problem in communications is the optimal discrimination of binary-phase-shift-keyed (BPSK) signals. A longstanding goal has been to reach the fundamental quantum limit, known as the Helstrom bound, for BPSK signals encoded in coherent states. However, due to technical constraints, proposals for reaching the bound remain impractical. In this letter we take an alternative approach: using only Gaussian optics - displaced squeezed states and homodyne detection - we achieve discrimination of BPSK signals with error rates below what can be achieved using coherent states and any quantum measurement.

papers.title: Statistical State Dynamics of Couette MHD Turbulence
papers.abstract: The roll streak structure (RSS) is ubiquitous in shear flow turbulence and is fundamental to the dynamics of the self-sustaining process (SSP) maintaining the turbulent state. The formation and maintenance of the RSS in wall-bounded shear flow suggest the presence of an underlying instability that has recently been identified using statistical state dynamics (SSD). Due to the parallelism between the Navier-Stokes equation and the induction equation, it is reasonable to inquire whether the RSS in wall-bounded shear flow has a counterpart in the MHD equations formulated as an SSD. In this work we show that this is the case and that an analytic solution for the composite velocitymagnetic field RSS in the MHD SSD also arises from an instability, that this instability equilibrates to either a fixed point or to a turbulent state, that these turbulent statistical equilibria may be self sustaining, and that both the fixed point and the turbulent states may correspond to large scale coherent dynamos.

papers.title: Transient Signal Propagation in Heterogeneous Networks under Various Inputs
papers.abstract: Transient signals in neural, biological and technological networks rarely follow a single route. Their strength and timing depend on where the input enters, on the intrinsic dynamics of each node visited, and on the feedforward and recurrent pathways that carry it. Previous theory has clarified important limits of signal propagation, but often for a single input type, averaged network structure, or asymptotic regimes. It has remained unclear how finite heterogeneous networks transform sustained, impulsive, finite-duration and stochastic inputs into node-resolved response timescales. Here, we develop a theory for network dynamics near stable operating states that answers this question. The framework identifies a canonical set of gains and timescales shared across deterministic and stochastic forcing and expresses them through matrix resolvents, spectra and directed walks. In positive, sufficiently damped networks, the walk representation gives a simple physical picture: response strength accumulates multiplicatively along a single path, whereas response time accumulates additively, through local intrinsic time constants. Competing pathways, feedback and inhibition further reshape propagation by amplifying, suppressing, reversing or delaying signals. We derive perturbative criteria that specify when these signatures, and the resulting node rankings, persist beyond the positive regime. Applied to a Wilson--Cowan model of the primate cortex, the theory links structural connectivity, excitatory--inhibitory balance and local biophysical timescales to hierarchical response timescales. Our results provide a mechanistic framework for input-dependent timescales in finite heterogeneous networks.

papers.title: Interpret Policies in Deep Reinforcement Learning using SILVER with RL-Guided Labeling: A Model-level Approach to High-dimensional and Multi-action Environments
papers.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) achieves remarkable performance but lacks interpretability, limiting trust in policy behavior. The existing SILVER framework (Li, Siddique, and Cao 2025) explains RL policy via Shapley-based regression but remains restricted to low-dimensional, binary-action domains. We propose SILVER with RL-guided labeling, an enhanced variant that extends SILVER to multi-action and high-dimensional environments by incorporating the RL policy's own action outputs into the boundary points identification. Our method first extracts compact feature representations from image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution, and then employs RL-guided labeling to generate behaviorally consistent boundary datasets. Surrogate models, such as decision trees and regression-based functions, are subsequently trained to interpret RL policy's decision structure. We evaluate the proposed framework on two Atari environments using three deep RL algorithms and conduct human-subject study to assess the clarity and trustworthiness of the derived interpretable policy. Results show that our approach maintains competitive task performance while substantially improving transparency and human understanding of agent behavior. This work advances explainable RL by transforming SILVER into a scalable and behavior-aware framework for interpreting deep RL agents in high-dimensional, multi-action settings.

papers.title: A Lichnerowicz equation in the Einstein-scalar field theory on non-CMC closed manifolds
papers.abstract: In the paper, we prove the existence of a positive and essentially bounded solution to a Lichnerowicz equation in the Einstein-scalar field theory on a closed manifold with non-constant mean curvature. In particular, the non-constant mean curvature gives rise to supercritical terms in the equation, on top of singular ones. We employ a recent fixed-point argument, which involves sub- and supersolutions. Additionally, we provide several conditions on the coefficients in the equation that prevent the existence of positive classical solutions.

papers.title: Energy calibration of bulk events in the BULLKID detector
papers.abstract: BULLKID is a cryogenic, solid-state detector designed for direct searches of particle Dark Matter candidates, with mass $\lesssim 1$ GeV/c$^2$, and coherent neutrino-nucleus scattering. It is based on an array of dice carved in 5 mm thick silicon crystal, sensed by phonon-mediated Kinetic Inductance Detectors. In previous works, the array was calibrated with bursts of optical photons, which are absorbed in the first hundreds nanometers of the dice and give rise to surface events. In this work, we present the reconstruction of bulk events through the 59.5 keV $\gamma$-ray generated by an $^{241}$Am source, which emulates more closely the interaction of Dark Matter and neutrinos. The peak resolution is $5\%~(\sigma)$ and its position is shifted by less than $10\%$ with respect to the optical calibration. We observe that the resolution is further improved by a factor $2$ combining the signal from neighboring dice. These results confirm the performance of the detector in view of the physics goals of the BULLKID-DM experiment for dark matter search.

papers.title: Blow-up rate for the subcritical semilinear heat equation in non-convex domains
papers.abstract: We consider the semilinear heat equation $u_t=\Delta u+|u|^{p-1} u$ in possibly non-convex and unbounded domains. Our main result shows the nonexistence of type II blow-up for possibly sign-changing solutions in the energy subcritical range $(n-2)p<n+2$. This resolves a long-standing open question dating back to the 1980s and also deduces the blow-up of the scaling critical norm.

papers.title: Generalized Centralizers and Polynomial Equivalence of Matrices: Answers to Questions of Dolinar, Guterman, Kuzma, and Markova
papers.abstract:
For $n	imes n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ over a field and a scalar $\omega
e0$, let $\mathcal C_\omega(A)=\{X:AX=\omega XA\}$. If $\omega$ is a root of unity of order $q\ge2$, then $\mathcal C_{\omega^j}(A)=\mathcal C_{\omega^j}(B)$ for all integers $j$ if and only if each of $A$ and $B$ is a polynomial in the other with exponents $\equiv1\pmod q$. Over algebraically closed fields, for $\omega
e1$, all $A$, and scalars $\varepsilon
e0$, we describe all $Y$ with $XY=\varepsilon YX$ for all $X\in\mathcal C_\omega(A)$. Let $a(\mu)$ be the size of the largest Jordan block of $A$ at $\mu$, or $0$ if there is none. If $\varepsilon$ is a power of $\omega$, all such $Y$ are polynomials in $A$ if and only if $a(\omega\mu)=a(\mu)$ for all $\mu
e0$, or this fails only at some $
u$ and at $\omega^{-1}
u$, where $A$ has a single largest Jordan block at $

u)=a(\omega^{-1}
u)=a(

e1$ has finite order, then for such $A$, $\mathcal C_\omega(A)=\mathcal C_\omega(B)$ exactly when $A$ and $B$ are polynomials in each other of this form. For all other $A$ some $B$ that is not a polynomial in $A$ satisfies $\mathcal C_\omega(A)=\mathcal C_\omega(B)$ if the field has more than $n^2+1$ elements. In the $\omega$-commuting digraph of Raja and Vaezpour, with an edge from $A$ to $B$ if $AB=\omega BA$, vertices with edges to and from the same vertices are twins. Over fields with more than $2n^2+1$ elements we determine the vertices $A$ whose twins are all polynomials in $A$, and describe these twins. We find all $A$, $B$, and $k\ge2$ for which the kernel of $(X\mapsto[A,X])^k$ is the set of $X$ with $[X,[X,\ldots,[X,B]\ldots]]=0$ ($k$ brackets), where $[X,Y]=XY-YX$. Apart from scalar $B$, this happens only in characteristic $

papers.title: The Economics of AI Foundation Models: Openness, Competition, and Governance
papers.abstract: Foundation model developers choose how open to make their models. Greater openness lowers downstream adaptation costs but can also make competing models easier to use. In a two-period model, an incumbent chooses its license fee and openness, a deployer adapts the model for users, and an entrant offers a competing model. Usage builds model-specific experience that lowers the deployer's future adaptation cost, creating a data flywheel that favors continued use of the incumbent. We identify conditions under which optimal openness falls and then rises as learning strengthens. The incumbent moves from full openness and a high fee to restricting openness for retention, then to a low fee that builds enough usage and experience to retain the deployer despite greater openness. A full-openness mandate can induce the incumbent to abandon this low-fee strategy. The higher fee can reduce first-period adaptation despite greater openness. An openness trap arises when this welfare loss exceeds the second-period gain from easier adaptation of the entrant's model. The trap can disappear when experience transfers across models. Full integration eliminates the fee between the incumbent and deployer but commits deployment to the incumbent, potentially forgoing a rival that is cheaper to adapt. Integration raises their joint profit, consumer surplus, and welfare when learning is sufficiently strong, but can lower them when learning is weak. A small usage subsidy can benefit both developers, the deployer, and consumers. It can instead induce a fee increase larger than the subsidy and reduced openness, raising the deployer's net payment per use and adaptation costs. The resulting reduction in adaptation lowers welfare even before subsidy expenditure is deducted. These findings connect AI policy to developers' pricing and openness responses and the portability of deployment experience.

papers.title: Classification of Transuranium Elements in Terms of `Winding' Numbers in the Bohr-Sommerfeld Model
papers.abstract: We revisit the Bohr-Sommerfeld atomic model to explore hydrogen-like ions of Uranium ($Z=92$), Oganesson ($Z=118$), and hypothetical superheavy elements beyond. Although superseded by the Dirac equation and modern quantum electrodynamics, the semiclassical approach offers a historically and pedagogically valuable perspective. Using the Sommerfeld fine structure formula and computer algebra methods, we demonstrate the appearance of self-intersecting orbits in super strong Coulomb fields, beginning with Oganesson and hypothetical elements up to $Z\le137$. These orbits can be classified by their `winding' numbers, providing a simple topological description of Coulomb field strength in this framework. Our results highlight a conceptual bridge between early quantum theory and modern superheavy element physics.

papers.title: A Subspecialty Diagnostic System Powered by Self-Supervised Learning for Cervical Histopathology
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major malignancy in women, with large-scale human papillomavirus-based screening generating a large volume of biopsies and, for advanced cases, surgical specimens, imposing an overwhelming diagnostic burden that necessitates precise histopathological evaluation. Although deep learning shows promise, general foundation models offer a broader reach but remain limited in capturing subspecialty-specific features and task adaptability. We introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, built upon the subspecialized dataset and developed through two synergistic pretraining stages: self-supervised learning on approximately 190 million tissue patches to build a cervical-specific feature extractor, and multimodal enhancement with 2.5 million image-text pairs, followed by diagnostic functions integration and downstream task enhancement. CerS-Path integrates eight functions -- across morphological diagnosis, predictive analytics, and multimodal tasks -- to cover the diagnostic workflow from biopsies to resection specimens. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate improved performance in cervical pathology in female patients, where CerS-Path outperforms state-of-the-art foundation models across 26 of 30 diagnostic tasks. Furthermore, in multicenter retrospective and prospective validation across six independent cohorts of women, CerS-Path achieves up to 99% sensitivity for clinically relevant lesion detection with acceptable specificity across sites, highlighting its potential for screening-derived histopathology and suitability for integration into high-volume diagnostic pathways.

papers.title: On the decomposition of the diagonal for n-fold hypersurfaces via cubic n-1-folds
